5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.Basic
6	
7	/-!
8	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
9	
10	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
11	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
12	
13	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
14	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
16	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
17	
18	## Proof sketch
19	
20	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
21	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
22	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
23	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
24	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
25	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
26	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
27	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
28	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
29	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
30	field is injective.
31	
32	Geometric reducedness enters only through `GeometricallyIntegral`; for the curve bundle of the
33	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace CommRingCat
43	
44	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
45	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
46	
47	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
48	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
49	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
50	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
51	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
52	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
53	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
54	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
55	  -- the codiagonal
56	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
57	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
58	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
59	  have : IsIso μ := by
60	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
61	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
62	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
63	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
64	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
65	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
66	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
67	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
68	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
69	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
71	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
72	
73	end CommRingCat
74	
75	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
76	
77	/-- Bundled variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.isField_of_universallyClosed`: if `X` is an integral
78	scheme, universally closed over the spectrum of a (bundled) commutative ring `R` that is a
79	field, then `Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field. -/
80	theorem isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (hR : IsField R)

Design decisions you own (document each in the module docstring):
- The exact formulation of "descent datum". The classical one: an isomorphism `φ : (B ⊗[A] M) ≃ₗ (M ⊗[A] B)` of `B ⊗[A] B`-modules (two `B`-actions) satisfying the cocycle condition over `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] B` and the unit/symmetry normalization. Getting the module structures right is the crux — consider mathlib's `TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule`, `IsBaseChange`, and how `Mathlib/RingTheory/...` phrases two-sided base change. Choose the phrasing that makes the EQUALIZER construction cleanest: `M₀ := {m : M | φ (1 ⊗ₜ m) = m ⊗ₜ 1}` (an `A`-submodule), with the descent theorem = the canonical map `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism.

188	Suppose we are given the following cartesian square:
189	```

201	  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ`, and `Uₓ` are all affine.

203	  injective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is compact, and `f` is flat.

Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model (e.g. Haiku) running in the
  background typically suffices, which is what the config is for:

  ```yaml
  references:
    transcription:
      harness: <optional harness>
      model: <cheap vision-capable model, e.g. a Haiku-class model>
  ```

  Don't pick the model inside the prompt; pin it in config so every transcription
  uses the same cheap vision model. When unset it falls back to the subagent/Ground
  harness.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:

+\section{The projective line: inputs for the finiteness argument}
+
+This section collects the facts about \(\PP^1\) and about morphisms over \(\Spec k\) that
+the finiteness argument of the next section consumes. It builds on the description of
+\(\PP^1\), its standard charts \(U_0, U_1\), the chart coordinates
+\(t_{ij} = X_j/X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\), and the section-ring identifications
+\(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\) developed in Chapter~\ref{chap:Curves}
+(Definitions~\ref{def:P1_chartOpen}, \ref{def:P1_chartCoord},
+\ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0}--\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}); the statements here
+are recorded in this chapter because they are private inputs of the finiteness glue rather
+than general theory of the projective line. Throughout, for a homogeneous \(f\) of positive
+degree we write \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) for the canonical map from the
+degree-zero localization to the sections over the basic open (an isomorphism).
+
+\begin{lemma}[Morphisms over the base intertwine the structure algebra maps]
+  \label{lem:appTop_map_appLE}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, let \(X, Y\) be schemes over \(\Spec k\) and let
+  \(\pi : X \to Y\) be a morphism compatible with the structure morphisms. For opens
+  \(U \subseteq Y\) and \(V \subseteq X\) with \(V \subseteq \pi^{-1}(U)\), the two
+  composite ring homomorphisms
+  \[
+    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, U)
+      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma(X, V)
+    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
+    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(X, \top) \to \Gamma(X, V)
+  \]
+  agree, where the unlabeled maps are induced by the structure morphisms and by
+  restriction.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Pulling back sections along \(\pi\) commutes with restriction, so the first composite is
+  the map on sections induced by \(\pi\) composed with the structure morphism of \(Y\),
+  restricted to \(V\); by compatibility this composite of morphisms is the structure
+  morphism of \(X\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[Pulling back the structure algebra map]
+  \label{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appLE_overAlgebraMap}
+  \uses{def:overAlgebraMap, lem:appTop_map_appLE}
+  \leanok
+  In the situation of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE}, for every \(r \in k\) the map
+  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(Y, U) \to \Gamma(X, V)\) sends the image of \(r\) under the
+  structure algebra map of \(Y\) (Definition~\ref{def:overAlgebraMap}) to the image of
+  \(r\) under the structure algebra map of \(X\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Evaluate the equality of ring homomorphisms of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE} at the section
+  corresponding to \(r\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The basic-open models lie over the base]
+  \label{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.awayι_structureMap}
+  \uses{def:P1_structureMap}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite of the affine
+  model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\) of the basic open \(D_+(f)\) with the structure
+  morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the algebra map
+  \(k \to A_{(f)}\). (This generalizes \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap} from the two
+  standard charts to all standard basic opens.)
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{def:P1_gradeZero}
+  As for \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap}: the canonical morphism
+  \(\Proj A \to \Spec A_0\), restricted to the affine model of a basic open, is induced by
+  the ring homomorphism \(A_0 \to A_{(f)}\), and composing with the isomorphism
+  \(k \cong A_0\) of \ref{def:P1_gradeZero} gives the claim.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The basic-open inclusion factors through its affine model]
+  \label{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_ι_eq}
+  \uses{def:P1}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The inclusion
+  \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) is the composite of the canonical identification
+  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) with the affine model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  The affine model is by construction an open immersion with image \(D_+(f)\), and the
+  canonical identification is the induced isomorphism onto the image; composing the two
+  recovers the inclusion.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The structure algebra map on a basic open]
+  \label{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
+  \uses{def:P1_structureMap, lem:P1_awayi_structureMap, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite
+  \[
+    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(\PP^1, \top) \to \Gamma\bigl(\PP^1, D_+(f)\bigr)
+  \]
+  (structure morphism on global sections, then restriction) is the composite of the
+  identification \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \cong k\), the algebra map \(k \to A_{(f)}\), and
+  the canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  By \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq} and \ref{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}, the composite of
+  the inclusion \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) with the structure morphism is the identification
+  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) followed by the morphism induced by \(k \to A_{(f)}\).
+  Taking global sections of this equality of scheme morphisms, and identifying the global
+  sections of the open subscheme \(D_+(f)\) with \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- under which
+  the map on sections induced by the identification with \(\Spec A_{(f)}\) becomes the
+  canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- yields the claim.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The distinguished fraction of a chart pair is the chart coordinate]
+  \label{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \uses{def:P1_chartCoord}
+  \leanok
+  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical degree-zero fraction
+  \(X_j^{\deg X_i} / X_i^{\deg X_j}\) attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\) of homogeneous
+  elements equals the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Both degrees are one, and a first power is the element itself.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap]
+  \label{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord}
+  \uses{def:P1_chartOpen, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq,
+    lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
+  \leanok
+  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), regard the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} \in A_{(X_i)}\) as a
+  section of the structure sheaf over the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i)\), via the canonical map
+  \(A_{(X_i)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\). Then the basic open of this section in the scheme
+  \(\PP^1\) --- the locus of \(U_i\) where it is invertible --- is the chart overlap:
+  \[
+    D(t_{ij}) \;=\; U_i \cap U_j .
+  \]
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  Both sides are open subsets of \(U_i\) (the basic open of a section over \(U_i\) is
+  contained in \(U_i\)), so it suffices to show that they have the same preimage under the
+  identification \(U_i \cong \Spec A_{(X_i)}\), and to transport the equality forward
+  along this open immersion. No stalks are involved: everything is transported through
+  the affine model.
+
+  On the one hand, the preimage of the basic open \(D(t_{ij})\) is the basic open of
+  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)}\) at the ring element \(t_{ij}\): under the identification of an
+  affine open with the spectrum of its section ring, scheme-level basic opens of sections
+  correspond to spectrum-level basic opens of ring elements.
+
+  On the other hand, the preimage of \(U_j = D_+(X_j)\) under the affine model
+  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) (through which the inclusion of \(U_i\) factors,
+  \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}) is the basic open at the canonical degree-zero fraction
+  attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\): a homogeneous prime avoiding \(X_i\) avoids
+  \(X_j\) exactly when the degree-zero fraction \(X_j/X_i\) is invertible in the
+  corresponding localization. By \ref{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq} this fraction is
+  \(t_{ij}\), so the preimage of \(U_i \cap U_j\) is again the basic open at
+  \(t_{ij}\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{lemma}[The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts]
+  \label{lem:P1_laurent_generators}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T,
+    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg,
+    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap}
+  \uses{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord}
+  \leanok
+  Under the identification
+  \(\gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\) of
+  \ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}:
+  \begin{enumerate}
+    \item \(T\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart coordinate
+      \(t_{01}\), regarded as a section over \(U_0\);
+    \item \(T^{-1}\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart
+      coordinate \(t_{10}\), regarded as a section over \(U_1\);
+    \item each scalar \(r \in k\) corresponds to the section over the overlap given by
+      the image of \(r\) under the algebra map \(k \to A_{(X_0X_1)}\).
+  \end{enumerate}
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{lem:P1_res_left, lem:P1_res_right}
+  (1) and (2): by \ref{lem:P1_res_left} (resp.\ \ref{lem:P1_res_right}), restriction from
+  the chart \(U_0\) (resp.\ \(U_1\)) to the overlap corresponds, under the
+  identifications \(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\), to \(t \mapsto T\) (resp.\
+  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\)); apply this to the sections corresponding to the polynomial
+  \(t\), which are the chart coordinates. (3): \(\gamma_{01}\) is built from the
+  \(k\)-algebra isomorphism \(\theta\) of \ref{def:P1_overlapAlgEquiv}, hence matches the
+  two algebra maps from \(k\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\section{Finiteness of the first cohomology}
+
+Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
+Chapter~\ref{chap:Algebra} along a finite morphism to the projective line yields the
+finiteness of \(H^1\). Classically this computation goes back to the explicit \v{C}ech
+computation of the cohomology of projective space --- for \(\PP^1\) itself, the
+description of \(H^1\) as the cokernel of the two-chart restriction-difference map into
+the Laurent ring, spanned by the finitely many ``negative'' monomials --- extended to a
+curve by pushing forward along a finite morphism; the two-lattice ladder is exactly the
+abstraction of that monomial bookkeeping.
+
+\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) along a finite morphism to the projective line]
+  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf, def:P1_structureMap}
+  \leanok
+  \source{hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243}
+  Let \(k\) be a field, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) a
+  finite morphism over \(k\) (its composite with the structure morphism of \(\PP^1\) is
+  the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\) is a finite
+  \(k\)-module.
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{lem:preimage_chart_affine, lem:preimage_chart_sup, lem:finite_app_overlap,
+    lem:P1_chartOpen_inf, thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv, def:TwoCover_diff, def:TwoCover_H1Cok,
+    def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_laurent_generators,
+    lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap, lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection,
+    thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord, cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}
+  Write \(U_0, U_1\) for the standard charts of \(\PP^1\) and set
+  \(V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)\).
+
+  (a) \emph{The cover and the cokernel.} Since \(\pi\) is finite, hence affine, the
+  \(V_i\) are affine opens of \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_affine}), and they cover
+  \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_sup}). By the two-affine-cover bridge
+  \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv},
+  \[
+    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;\cong\;
+      N \big/ \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}),
+    \qquad N := \Gamma(X, V_0 \cap V_1),
+  \]
+  with \(\mathrm{diff}(s_0, s_1) = s_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1} - s_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\)
+  (\ref{def:TwoCover_diff}). It therefore suffices to prove that this quotient is a
+  finite \(k\)-module.
+
+  (b) \emph{The Laurent module structure.} Preimages commute with intersections, and
+  \(U_0 \cap U_1 = D_+(X_0X_1)\) (\ref{lem:P1_chartOpen_inf}), so
+  \(V_0 \cap V_1 = \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\). Make \(N\) an algebra over the Laurent
+  polynomial ring via the composite
+  \[
+    k[T, T^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{01}^{-1}\ } \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1)
+      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma\bigl(X, \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\bigr) = N
+  \]
+  (\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}). This structure is compatible with the \(k\)-module
+  structure of \(N\): a scalar \(r \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) corresponds under \(\gamma_{01}\) to
+  the image of \(r\) under the algebra map into the overlap ring
+  (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(3)), which is the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\)
+  on \(U_0 \cap U_1\) (\ref{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}), and \(\pi\) pulls
+  the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\) back to that of \(X\)
+  (\ref{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}). Hence the \(k\)-module structure of \(N\) is the
+  restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-structure along the canonical map
+  \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\).
+
+  (c) \emph{Module-finiteness over the Laurent ring.} Since \(\pi\) is finite and
+  \(U_0 \cap U_1\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\), the map
+  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \to N\) is module-finite
+  (\ref{lem:finite_app_overlap}); composing with the isomorphism \(\gamma_{01}^{-1}\),
+  \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module.
+
+  (d) \emph{The two lattices, and the range of the difference map.} Let
+  \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be the images of the (\(k\)-linear) restriction maps
+  \(\Gamma(X, V_0) \to N\) and \(\Gamma(X, V_1) \to N\). Then
+  \(\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}) = Q_0 + Q_1\): every value
+  \(s_0| - s_1|\) of \(\mathrm{diff}\) is the sum of \(s_0| \in Q_0\) and
+  \(-(s_1|) = (-s_1)| \in Q_1\); conversely \(s_0| = \mathrm{diff}(s_0, 0) \) and
+  \(s_1| = \mathrm{diff}(0, -s_1)\) exhibit every element of \(Q_0\) and of \(Q_1\) as a
+  value of \(\mathrm{diff}\) --- the sign is absorbed because \(Q_1\) is the image of a
+  linear map.
+
+  (e) \emph{Lattice stability.} Let
+  \(\tau_0 = \pi^\sharp(t_{01}) \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) and
+  \(\tau_1 = \pi^\sharp(t_{10}) \in \Gamma(X, V_1)\) be the pullbacks of the chart
+  coordinates, regarded as sections over the charts
+  (Definition~\ref{def:P1_chartCoord}). By \ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(1) and the
+  compatibility of \(\pi^\sharp\) with restriction, \(T\) acts on \(N\) as
+  multiplication by \(\tau_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\); symmetrically \(T^{-1}\) acts as
+  multiplication by \(\tau_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\) (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(2)).
+  Hence \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): for \(s \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\),
+  \[
+    T \cdot s|_{V_0 \cap V_1} \;=\; \tau_0|\cdot s| \;=\; (\tau_0 s)|_{V_0 \cap V_1}
+      \;\in\; Q_0,
+  \]
+  and symmetrically \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\).
+
+  (f) \emph{Absorption up to powers.} The overlap is a basic open inside each chart
+  preimage: pulling back the identity \(D(t_{ij}) = U_i \cap U_j\) of
+  \ref{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord} along \(\pi\) (basic opens of sections pull back to
+  basic opens of the pulled-back sections) gives
+  \[
+    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_0) \subseteq V_0,
+    \qquad
+    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_1) \subseteq V_1 .
+  \]
+  Since \(V_0\) is affine and \(V_0 \cap V_1\) is its basic open defined by \(\tau_0\),
+  restriction identifies \(N\) with the localization of \(\Gamma(X, V_0)\) at the powers
+  of \(\tau_0\) (quasi-coherence of the structure sheaf). Hence for every \(n \in N\)
+  there are \(m \ge 0\) and \(a \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) with
+  \(n \cdot (\tau_0|)^m = a|\), i.e.\ \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\). Symmetrically, every
+  \(n \in N\) satisfies \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\) for some \(m \ge 0\).
+
+  (g) \emph{The ladder.} By (b), (c), (e) and (f), the module \(N\) over
+  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) with the \(k\)-submodules \(Q_0, Q_1\) satisfies all hypotheses of the
+  two-lattice finiteness theorem in its localization form via powers of the generator
+  (\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}); hence \(N/(Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module. By
+  (d) this quotient is \(N/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff})\), and by (a) it is
+  \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\).
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) of the curve]
+  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf}
+  \leanok
+  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth curve over \(k\) (proper, smooth of relative
+  dimension one, geometrically irreducible). Then
+  \(H^1\bigl(C, \struct{C/k}\bigr)\) is a finite \(k\)-module; equivalently, it is a
+  finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space.
+\end{theorem}
+\begin{proof}
+  \leanok
+  \uses{thm:exists_finite_toP1, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
+  By \ref{thm:exists_finite_toP1} there is a finite morphism \(\pi : C \to \PP^1\) over
+  \(k\); apply \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{remark}[The genus is the dimension of a finite-dimensional space]
+  \label{rem:genus_finite}
+  \uses{def:genus, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
+  \leanok
+  For a smooth curve \(C\) over \(k\), the genus of Definition~\ref{def:genus} is the
+  \(k\)-dimension of \(H^1(C, \struct C)\), which by
+  \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one} is a finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space; the
+  genus is therefore a well-defined natural number, attained as the cardinality of any
+  basis.
+\end{remark}

/-
Copyright (c) 2025 Andrew Yang. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Andrew Yang
-/
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Limits
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Cartesian.Mon
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Grp

/-!
# Yoneda embedding of `Grp C`

We show that group objects are exactly those whose yoneda presheaf is a presheaf of groups,
by constructing the yoneda embedding `Grp C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{v}` and
showing that it is fully faithful and its (essential) image is the representable functors.
-/

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists Field

open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory Limits Opposite CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj

namespace CategoryTheory
universe w v u
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [CartesianMonoidalCategory C]
  {M G H X Y : C} [MonObj M] [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H]

variable (X) in
/-- If `X` represents a presheaf of monoids, then `X` is a monoid object. -/
@[to_additive (attr := implicit_reducible)
/-- If `X` represents a presheaf of additive monoids, then `X` is an additive monoid object. -/]
def GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) (α : (F ⋙ forget _).RepresentableBy X) :
    GrpObj X where
  __ := MonObj.ofRepresentableBy X (F ⋙ forget₂ GrpCat MonCat) α
  inv := α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv (𝟙 _))⁻¹
  left_inv := by
    change lift (α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv (𝟙 X))⁻¹) (𝟙 X) ≫
      α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (fst X X) * α.homEquiv' (snd X X)) =
        toUnit X ≫ α.homEquiv'.symm 1
    apply α.homEquiv'.injective
    simp only [α.homEquiv'_comp, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, map_mul, map_one]
    simp only [← α.homEquiv'_comp, lift_fst, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, lift_snd]
    exact inv_mul_cancel (α.homEquiv (𝟙 X))
  right_inv := by
    change lift (𝟙 X) (α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (𝟙 X))⁻¹) ≫
      α.homEquiv'.symm (α.homEquiv' (fst X X) * α.homEquiv' (snd X X)) =
        toUnit X ≫ α.homEquiv'.symm 1
    apply α.homEquiv'.injective
    simp only [α.homEquiv'_comp, Equiv.apply_symm_apply, map_mul, map_one]
    simp only [← α.homEquiv'_comp]
    simp

/-- If `G` is a group object, then `Hom(X, G)` has a group structure. -/
@[to_additive
/-- If `G` is an additive group object, then `Hom(X, G)` has an additive group structure. -/]
abbrev Hom.group : Group (X ⟶ G) where
  inv f := f ≫ ι
  inv_mul_cancel f := calc
    lift (f ≫ ι) f ≫ μ
    _ = (f ≫ lift ι (𝟙 G)) ≫ μ := by simp
    _ = toUnit X ≫ η := by rw [Category.assoc]; simp

scoped[CategoryTheory.MonObj] attribute [instance] Hom.group
scoped[CategoryTheory.AddMonObj] attribute [instance] Hom.addGroup

@[to_additive]
lemma Hom.inv_def (f : X ⟶ G) : f⁻¹ = f ≫ ι := rfl

variable (G) in
/-- If `G` is a group object, then `Hom(-, G)` is a presheaf of groups. -/
@[to_additive (attr := simps)
/-- If `G` is an additive group object, then `Hom(-, G)` is a presheaf of additive groups. -/]
def yonedaGrpObj : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{v} where
  obj X := GrpCat.of (unop X ⟶ G)
  map φ := GrpCat.ofHom ((yonedaMonObj G).map φ).hom

variable (G) in

    40	/-! ### Pulling back the structure algebra map along a morphism over `Spec k` -/
    41	
    42	variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
    43	
    44	/-- For a morphism `π : X ⟶ Y` of schemes over `Spec k` (compatibly with the structure
    45	morphisms), pulling back sections along `π` intertwines the structure algebra maps, in
    46	morphism form: restricting the structure sections of `Y` from `⊤` to `U` and applying
    47	`π.appLE U V e` equals the structure sections of `X` restricted from `⊤` to `V`. -/
    48	lemma Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    49	    [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] (π : X ⟶ Y) (hπ : π ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) = X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    50	    {U : Y.Opens} {V : X.Opens} (e : V ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    51	    (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤)).op ≫
    52	        π.appLE U V e =
    53	      (X ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op := by
    54	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
    55	  change (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)).appTop ≫ π.appTop ≫
    56	      X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op = _
    57	  rw [← Category.assoc, ← Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, hπ]
    58	
    59	/-- Elementwise form of `Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE`, phrased through
    60	`Scheme.overAlgebraMap`: `π` pulls the structure algebra map of `Y` back to that of `X`. -/
    61	lemma Scheme.Hom.appLE_overAlgebraMap {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    62	    [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] (π : X ⟶ Y) (hπ : π ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) = X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    63	    {U : Y.Opens} {V : X.Opens} (e : V ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ U) (r : k) :
    64	    (π.appLE U V e).hom (Y.overAlgebraMap k U r) = X.overAlgebraMap k V r := by
    65	  have h := π.appTop_map_appLE hπ e
    66	  have h2 := congr((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ $h)
    67	  exact congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $h2) r)
    68	
    69	end OverAlgebraMap

    73	/-! ### The chart coordinates of `ℙ¹`: structure map and basic opens -/
    74	
    75	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
    76	
    77	/-- The standard grading of `k[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 k`. -/
    78	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k
    79	
    80	/-- The affine chart inclusions `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_f)₀ ⟶ ℙ¹` are morphisms over `Spec k`,
    81	for any homogeneous `f` of positive degree (generalizing `P1.chartι_structureMap`). -/
    82	theorem awayι_structureMap {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ} (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m)
    83	    (hm : 0 < m) :
    84	    Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm ≫ structureMap k =
    85	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f))) := by
    86	  change Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm ≫
    87	      (Proj.toSpecZero 𝒜 ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (𝒜 0)))) = _
    88	  rw [Proj.awayι_toSpecZero_assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    89	  rfl
    90	
    91	/-- The inclusion of a standard basic open of `ℙ¹` factors through its affine model. -/
    92	theorem basicOpen_ι_eq {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ} (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) :
    93	    (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι = Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f ≫ Proj.awayι 𝒜 f f_deg hm := by
    94	  rw [← Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec_inv_ι 𝒜 f f_deg hm, ← Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec_hom 𝒜 f f_deg hm,
    95	    Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
    96	
    97	/-- The structure algebra map of `ℙ¹` restricted to a standard basic open `D₊(f)` is the
    98	composite `Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k → (k[X₀,X₁]_f)₀ → Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(f))`, in morphism form. -/
    99	theorem structureMap_appTop_awayToSection {f : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k} {m : ℕ}
   100	    (f_deg : f ∈ 𝒜 m) (hm : 0 < m) :
   101	    (structureMap k).appTop ≫
   102	        (P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⊤)).op =
   103	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).hom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f)) ≫
   104	        Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f := by
   105	  have h1 : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι ≫ structureMap k =
   106	      Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f ≫
   107	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 f))) := by
   108	    rw [basicOpen_ι_eq k f_deg hm, Category.assoc, awayι_structureMap k f_deg hm]
   109	  have h2 := congrArg Scheme.Hom.appTop h1
   110	  rw [Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop, Scheme.Hom.comp_appTop] at h2
   111	  have h3 : (Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 f).appTop =
   112	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).hom ≫ Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 f ≫
   113	        (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.inv :=
   114	    Proj.basicOpenToSpec_app_top 𝒜 f
   115	  rw [h3, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality_assoc] at h2
   116	  have h4 : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).ι.appTop ≫ (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.hom =
   117	      (P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f ≤ ⊤)).op := by
   118	    rw [Scheme.Opens.ι_appTop, Scheme.Opens.topIso_hom, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp]
   119	    exact congrArg _ (congrArg Quiver.Hom.op (Subsingleton.elim _ _))
   120	  have h5 := congr($h2 ≫ (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 f).topIso.hom)
   121	  rw [Category.assoc, h4] at h5
   122	  simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id] at h5
   123	  exact h5
   124	
   125	/-- `g^d/f^e = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`: the mathlib localization element of the pair `(Xᵢ, Xⱼ)` is the chart
   126	coordinate (generalizing `P1.isLocalizationElem_eq` to both charts). -/
   127	theorem isLocalizationElem_X_eq (i j : Fin 2) :
   128	    Away.isLocalizationElem (X_mem k i) (X_mem k j) = chartCoord k i j := by
   129	  rw [Away.isLocalizationElem, chartCoord_eq]
   130	  congr 1
   131	  exact pow_one _
   132	
   133	/-- **The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap**: on `ℙ¹`, the scheme-level basic open of
   134	the section `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ ∈ Γ(D₊(Xᵢ))` is the chart overlap `D₊(Xᵢ) ⊓ D₊(Xⱼ)`. -/
   135	theorem basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord (i j : Fin 2) :
   136	    (P1 k).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
   137	      chartOpen k i ⊓ chartOpen k j := by
   138	  change (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) =
   139	    Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j)
   140	  have hpre : (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ
   141	        ((Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))) =
   142	      (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := by
   143	    rw [← Scheme.Opens.toSpecΓ_preimage_basicOpen]
   144	    conv_rhs => rw [basicOpen_ι_eq k (X_mem k i) one_pos]
   145	    change _ = Proj.basicOpenToSpec 𝒜 (X i) ⁻¹ᵁ
   146	      (Proj.awayι 𝒜 (X i) (X_mem k i) one_pos ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j))
   147	    rw [Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen 𝒜 (X_mem k i) one_pos (X_mem k j) one_pos,
   148	      isLocalizationElem_X_eq k i j]
   149	    rfl
   150	  have himg := congrArg (fun W => (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i)).ι ''ᵁ W) hpre
   151	  simp only [Scheme.Hom.image_preimage_eq_opensRange_inf, Scheme.Opens.opensRange_ι]
   152	    at himg
   153	  have hle : (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) ≤
   154	      Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) := (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen_le _
   155	  calc (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j))
   156	      = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓
   157	          (Proj 𝒜).basicOpen ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X i)).hom (chartCoord k i j)) :=
   158	        (inf_eq_right.mpr hle).symm
   159	    _ = Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X i) ⊓ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X j) := himg
   160

   162	
   163	/-- Under the overlap identification, `T` is the restriction to the overlap of the chart-0
   164	coordinate `X₁/X₀ ∈ Γ(D₊(X₀))`. -/
   165	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T :

   167	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_left k)).op).hom
   168	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
   169	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
   170	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_left, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
   171	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapLeft, awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord k fin_zero_ne_one,
   172	    Polynomial.toLaurent_X]

   176	theorem overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg :
   177	    (overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1)) =
   178	      ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (overlap_le_right k)).op).hom
   179	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
   180	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective
   181	  rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply, res_awayToSection_right, overlapSectionsEquiv_awayToSection,
   182	    overlapAlgEquiv_awayToOverlapRight_chartCoord]
   183	
   184	/-- The overlap identification matches the algebra map of the homogeneous localization

   188	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) r) := by
   189	  apply (overlapSectionsEquiv k).injective

8	/-!
9	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
10	
11	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
12	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
13	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
14	modules:
15	
16	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
19	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
20	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
21	function spaces.
22	
23	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
24	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
25	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
26	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
28	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
33	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
34	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
35	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
36	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
37	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
38	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
39	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
40	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
41	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
42	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
43	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
44	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
45	
46	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
47	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
48	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
49	-/
50

55	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

57	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

61	section Square
62	
63	variable (X : Scheme.{u}) (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
64	
65	/-- The Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the small Zariski site of a
66	scheme `X`, for two opens covering `X`. -/
67	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverSquare (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
68	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)).MayerVietorisSquare :=
69	  Opens.mayerVietorisSquare'
70	    { X₁ := U₀ ⊓ U₁
71	      X₂ := U₀
72	      X₃ := U₁
73	      X₄ := ⊤
74	      f₁₂ := homOfLE inf_le_left
75	      f₁₃ := homOfLE inf_le_right
76	      f₂₄ := homOfLE le_top
77	      f₃₄ := homOfLE le_top
78	      fac := Subsingleton.elim _ _ } hcov.symm rfl
79	
80	end Square

82	section GeneralCoefficients
83	
84	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
85	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
86	
87	/-- **The two-cover H¹ computation, general coefficients.** For a sheaf `F` of
88	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site of `X`, two opens with `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` and
89	vanishing `H¹'(U₀, F)`, `H¹'(U₁, F)`, the degree-one cohomology of the site is the
90	cokernel of the restriction-difference map `F(U₀) × F(U₁) → F(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`. -/
91	noncomputable def Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv
92	    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat)) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
93	    (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
94	    [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1)] [Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1)] :
95	    Sheaf.HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k]
96	      (F.obj.obj (op (U₀ ⊓ U₁)) ⧸
97	        LinearMap.range ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff F)) :=
98	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₂ 1) :=
99	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₀ 1))
100	  letI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).X₃ 1) :=
101	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' F U₁ 1))
102	  (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) F 1).trans
103	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).h1LinearEquiv F).symm
104	
105	end GeneralCoefficients

107	namespace TwoCover
108	
109	variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
110	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
111	
112	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
113	
114	/-- The restriction-difference map `Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`,
115	`(s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁} - s₁|_{U₀ ⊓ U₁}` (see `TwoCover.diff_apply`), with the
116	`k`-module structures of `Scheme.overModule`. -/
117	noncomputable def diff : (Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) →ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
118	  ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom.comp
119	      (LinearMap.fst k _ _) -
120	    ((X.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom.comp
121	      (LinearMap.snd k _ _)
122	
123	lemma diff_apply (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
124	    diff k X U₀ U₁ t = X.resHom inf_le_left t.1 - X.resHom inf_le_right t.2 :=
125	  rfl
126	
127	/-- The two-cover difference map is the Mayer–Vietoris restriction-difference map of the
128	associated square. -/
129	lemma diff_eq_moduleDiff (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) :
130	    diff k X U₀ U₁ = (X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDiff (X.moduleKSheaf k) :=
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- **The two-cover H¹ cokernel carrier**: the cokernel of the restriction-difference
134	map, `Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range (TwoCover.diff)`. For `U₀, U₁` an affine open cover this is
135	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪)` (see `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`); it is a plain quotient of section modules, so
136	`Module.finrank` arguments can be run on it directly. -/
137	noncomputable abbrev H1Cok : Type u :=
138	  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ LinearMap.range (diff k X U₀ U₁)
139	
140	/-- A section extending to `U₀` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
141	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_left (t : Γ(X, U₀)) :
142	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_left t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
143	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
144	  exact ⟨(t, 0), by rw [diff_apply]; simp⟩
145	
146	/-- A section extending to `U₁` has vanishing class in `H1Cok`. -/
147	lemma h1Cok_mk_resHom_right (t : Γ(X, U₁)) :
148	    (Submodule.Quotient.mk (X.resHom inf_le_right t) : H1Cok k X U₀ U₁) = 0 := by
149	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
150	  refine ⟨(0, -t), ?_⟩
151	  rw [diff_apply]
152	  simp

154	section Bridge
155	
156	variable (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
157	
158	/-- The two-cover connecting map: the degree-one cohomology class of a section on the
159	overlap `U₀ ⊓ U₁`, in the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule` of the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
160	noncomputable def delta :
161	    Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 :=
162	  ((Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens))
163	      (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1).symm.toLinearMap).comp
164	    ((X.twoCoverSquare U₀ U₁ hcov).moduleDelta (X.moduleKSheaf k))
165	
166	/-- The connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes. -/
167	lemma delta_diff (t : Γ(X, U₀) × Γ(X, U₁)) :
168	    delta k X U₀ U₁ hcov (diff k X U₀ U₁ t) = 0 := by

101	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/

104	  exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite (exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1 C.hom)

107	
108	The next wave feeds these to the two-lattice/Mayer–Vietoris finiteness argument: the
109	preimages of the two standard charts form an affine cover of `C`, with section rings
110	module-finite over `k[t]`. Everything here only needs `π` finite (indeed mostly just
111	affine), not how it was constructed. -/

116	
117	/-- The preimage of each standard chart of `ℙ¹` under an affine (e.g. finite) morphism is an
118	affine open. -/
119	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
120	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=
121	  (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i).preimage π
122	
123	/-- The preimages of the two standard charts of `ℙ¹` cover the source. -/
124	theorem preimage_chartOpen_sup :
125	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 = ⊤ := by
126	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
127	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
128	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
129	    trivial
130	  rw [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup] at h ⊢
131	  exact h
132	
133	/-- For a finite morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, the section ring of the preimage of a standard chart
134	is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (that is, over `k[t]`, via
135	`P1.chartSectionsEquiv₀`/`₁`). -/
136	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
137	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
138	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)
139

141	overlap is module-finite over the section ring of the overlap (that is, over the Laurent
142	polynomial ring, via `P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`). -/

144	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
145	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
146	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)
147

1160	\section{The projective line: inputs for the finiteness argument}
1161	
1162	This section collects the facts about \(\PP^1\) and about morphisms over \(\Spec k\) that
1163	the finiteness argument of the next section consumes. It builds on the description of
1164	\(\PP^1\), its standard charts \(U_0, U_1\), the chart coordinates
1165	\(t_{ij} = X_j/X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\), and the section-ring identifications
1166	\(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\) developed in Chapter~\ref{chap:Curves}
1167	(Definitions~\ref{def:P1_chartOpen}, \ref{def:P1_chartCoord},
1168	\ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0}--\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}); the statements here
1169	are recorded in this chapter because they are private inputs of the finiteness glue rather
1170	than general theory of the projective line. Throughout, for a homogeneous \(f\) of positive
1171	degree we write \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) for the canonical map from the
1172	degree-zero localization to the sections over the basic open (an isomorphism).
1173	
1174	\begin{lemma}[Morphisms over the base intertwine the structure algebra maps]
1175	  \label{lem:appTop_map_appLE}
1176	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appTop_map_appLE}
1177	  \leanok
1178	  Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, let \(X, Y\) be schemes over \(\Spec k\) and let
1179	  \(\pi : X \to Y\) be a morphism compatible with the structure morphisms. For opens
1180	  \(U \subseteq Y\) and \(V \subseteq X\) with \(V \subseteq \pi^{-1}(U)\), the two
1181	  composite ring homomorphisms
1182	  \[
1183	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, U)
1184	      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma(X, V)
1185	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
1186	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(X, \top) \to \Gamma(X, V)
1187	  \]
1188	  agree, where the unlabeled maps are induced by the structure morphisms and by
1189	  restriction.
1190	\end{lemma}
1191	\begin{proof}
1192	  \leanok
1193	  Pulling back sections along \(\pi\) commutes with restriction, so the first composite is
1194	  the map on sections induced by \(\pi\) composed with the structure morphism of \(Y\),
1195	  restricted to \(V\); by compatibility this composite of morphisms is the structure
1196	  morphism of \(X\).
1197	\end{proof}

1199	\begin{lemma}[Pulling back the structure algebra map]
1200	  \label{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}
1201	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.appLE_overAlgebraMap}
1202	  \uses{def:overAlgebraMap, lem:appTop_map_appLE}
1203	  \leanok
1204	  In the situation of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE}, for every \(r \in k\) the map
1205	  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(Y, U) \to \Gamma(X, V)\) sends the image of \(r\) under the

1208	\end{lemma}

1210	  \leanok

1212	  corresponding to \(r\).
1213	\end{proof}

1215	\begin{lemma}[The basic-open models lie over the base]
1216	  \label{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}
1217	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.awayι_structureMap}
1218	  \uses{def:P1_structureMap}

1220	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite of the affine
1221	  model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\) of the basic open \(D_+(f)\) with the structure
1222	  morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the algebra map
1223	  \(k \to A_{(f)}\). (This generalizes \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap} from the two
1224	  standard charts to all standard basic opens.)
1225	\end{lemma}

1230	  \(\Proj A \to \Spec A_0\), restricted to the affine model of a basic open, is induced by
1231	  the ring homomorphism \(A_0 \to A_{(f)}\), and composing with the isomorphism
1232	  \(k \cong A_0\) of \ref{def:P1_gradeZero} gives the claim.
1233	\end{proof}

1235	\begin{lemma}[The basic-open inclusion factors through its affine model]
1236	  \label{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
1237	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_ι_eq}
1238	  \uses{def:P1}
1239	  \leanok
1240	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The inclusion
1241	  \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) is the composite of the canonical identification
1242	  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) with the affine model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\).
1243	\end{lemma}
1244	\begin{proof}
1245	  \leanok
1246	  The affine model is by construction an open immersion with image \(D_+(f)\), and the
1247	  canonical identification is the induced isomorphism onto the image; composing the two
1248	  recovers the inclusion.
1249	\end{proof}

1251	\begin{lemma}[The structure algebra map on a basic open]
1252	  \label{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
1253	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}
1254	  \uses{def:P1_structureMap, lem:P1_awayi_structureMap, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}
1255	  \leanok
1256	  Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite
1257	  \[
1258	    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(\PP^1, \top) \to \Gamma\bigl(\PP^1, D_+(f)\bigr)
1259	  \]
1260	  (structure morphism on global sections, then restriction) is the composite of the
1261	  identification \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \cong k\), the algebra map \(k \to A_{(f)}\), and
1262	  the canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\).
1263	\end{lemma}
1264	\begin{proof}
1265	  \leanok
1266	  By \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq} and \ref{lem:P1_awayi_structureMap}, the composite of
1267	  the inclusion \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) with the structure morphism is the identification
1268	  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) followed by the morphism induced by \(k \to A_{(f)}\).
1269	  Taking global sections of this equality of scheme morphisms, and identifying the global
1270	  sections of the open subscheme \(D_+(f)\) with \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- under which
1271	  the map on sections induced by the identification with \(\Spec A_{(f)}\) becomes the
1272	  canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\) --- yields the claim.
1273	\end{proof}
1274	
1275	\begin{lemma}[The distinguished fraction of a chart pair is the chart coordinate]
1276	  \label{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1277	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1278	  \uses{def:P1_chartCoord}
1279	  \leanok
1280	  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical degree-zero fraction
1281	  \(X_j^{\deg X_i} / X_i^{\deg X_j}\) attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\) of homogeneous
1282	  elements equals the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).
1283	\end{lemma}
1284	\begin{proof}
1285	  \leanok
1286	  Both degrees are one, and a first power is the element itself.
1287	\end{proof}
1288	
1289	\begin{theorem}[The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap]
1290	  \label{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord}
1291	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord}
1292	  \uses{def:P1_chartOpen, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq,
1293	    lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq}
1294	  \leanok
1295	  For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), regard the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} \in A_{(X_i)}\) as a
1296	  section of the structure sheaf over the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i)\), via the canonical map
1297	  \(A_{(X_i)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\). Then the basic open of this section in the scheme
1298	  \(\PP^1\) --- the locus of \(U_i\) where it is invertible --- is the chart overlap:
1299	  \[
1300	    D(t_{ij}) \;=\; U_i \cap U_j .
1301	  \]
1302	\end{theorem}
1303	\begin{proof}
1304	  \leanok
1305	  Both sides are open subsets of \(U_i\) (the basic open of a section over \(U_i\) is
1306	  contained in \(U_i\)), so it suffices to show that they have the same preimage under the
1307	  identification \(U_i \cong \Spec A_{(X_i)}\), and to transport the equality forward
1308	  along this open immersion. No stalks are involved: everything is transported through
1309	  the affine model.
1310	
1311	  On the one hand, the preimage of the basic open \(D(t_{ij})\) is the basic open of
1312	  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)}\) at the ring element \(t_{ij}\): under the identification of an
1313	  affine open with the spectrum of its section ring, scheme-level basic opens of sections
1314	  correspond to spectrum-level basic opens of ring elements.
1315	
1316	  On the other hand, the preimage of \(U_j = D_+(X_j)\) under the affine model
1317	  \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) (through which the inclusion of \(U_i\) factors,
1318	  \ref{lem:P1_basicOpen_iota_eq}) is the basic open at the canonical degree-zero fraction
1319	  attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\): a homogeneous prime avoiding \(X_i\) avoids
1320	  \(X_j\) exactly when the degree-zero fraction \(X_j/X_i\) is invertible in the
1321	  corresponding localization. By \ref{lem:P1_isLocalizationElem_X_eq} this fraction is
1322	  \(t_{ij}\), so the preimage of \(U_i \cap U_j\) is again the basic open at
1323	  \(t_{ij}\).
1324	\end{proof}
1325	
1326	\begin{lemma}[The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts]
1327	  \label{lem:P1_laurent_generators}
1328	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T,
1329	    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg,
1330	    AlgebraicGeometry.P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap}
1331	  \uses{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord}
1332	  \leanok
1333	  Under the identification
1334	  \(\gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\) of
1335	  \ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}:
1336	  \begin{enumerate}
1337	    \item \(T\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart coordinate
1338	      \(t_{01}\), regarded as a section over \(U_0\);
1339	    \item \(T^{-1}\) corresponds to the restriction to the overlap of the chart
1340	      coordinate \(t_{10}\), regarded as a section over \(U_1\);
1341	    \item each scalar \(r \in k\) corresponds to the section over the overlap given by
1342	      the image of \(r\) under the algebra map \(k \to A_{(X_0X_1)}\).
1343	  \end{enumerate}
1344	\end{lemma}
1345	\begin{proof}
1346	  \leanok
1347	  \uses{lem:P1_res_left, lem:P1_res_right}
1348	  (1) and (2): by \ref{lem:P1_res_left} (resp.\ \ref{lem:P1_res_right}), restriction from
1349	  the chart \(U_0\) (resp.\ \(U_1\)) to the overlap corresponds, under the
1350	  identifications \(\gamma_0, \gamma_1, \gamma_{01}\), to \(t \mapsto T\) (resp.\
1351	  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\)); apply this to the sections corresponding to the polynomial
1352	  \(t\), which are the chart coordinates. (3): \(\gamma_{01}\) is built from the
1353	  \(k\)-algebra isomorphism \(\theta\) of \ref{def:P1_overlapAlgEquiv}, hence matches the
1354	  two algebra maps from \(k\).
1355	\end{proof}
1356	
1357	\section{Finiteness of the first cohomology}
1358	
1359	Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
1360	Chapter~\ref{chap:Algebra} along a finite morphism to the projective line yields the
1361	finiteness of \(H^1\). Classically this computation goes back to the explicit \v{C}ech
1362	computation of the cohomology of projective space --- for \(\PP^1\) itself, the
1363	description of \(H^1\) as the cokernel of the two-chart restriction-difference map into
1364	the Laurent ring, spanned by the finitely many ``negative'' monomials --- extended to a
1365	curve by pushing forward along a finite morphism; the two-lattice ladder is exactly the
1366	abstraction of that monomial bookkeeping.
1367	
1368	\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) along a finite morphism to the projective line]
1369	  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
1370	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
1371	  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf, def:P1_structureMap}
1372	  \leanok
1373	  \source{hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0242, hartshorne-algebraic-geometry:page-0243}
1374	  Let \(k\) be a field, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) a
1375	  finite morphism over \(k\) (its composite with the structure morphism of \(\PP^1\) is
1376	  the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\) is a finite
1377	  \(k\)-module.
1378	\end{theorem}
1379	\begin{proof}
1380	  \leanok
1381	  \uses{lem:preimage_chart_affine, lem:preimage_chart_sup, lem:finite_app_overlap,
1382	    lem:P1_chartOpen_inf, thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv, def:TwoCover_diff, def:TwoCover_H1Cok,
1383	    def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv, def:P1_chartCoord, lem:P1_laurent_generators,
1384	    lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap, lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection,
1385	    thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord, cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}
1386	  Write \(U_0, U_1\) for the standard charts of \(\PP^1\) and set
1387	  \(V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)\).
1388	
1389	  (a) \emph{The cover and the cokernel.} Since \(\pi\) is finite, hence affine, the
1390	  \(V_i\) are affine opens of \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_affine}), and they cover
1391	  \(X\) (\ref{lem:preimage_chart_sup}). By the two-affine-cover bridge
1392	  \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv},
1393	  \[
1394	    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;\cong\;
1395	      N \big/ \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}),
1396	    \qquad N := \Gamma(X, V_0 \cap V_1),
1397	  \]
1398	  with \(\mathrm{diff}(s_0, s_1) = s_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1} - s_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\)
1399	  (\ref{def:TwoCover_diff}). It therefore suffices to prove that this quotient is a
1400	  finite \(k\)-module.
1401	
1402	  (b) \emph{The Laurent module structure.} Preimages commute with intersections, and
1403	  \(U_0 \cap U_1 = D_+(X_0X_1)\) (\ref{lem:P1_chartOpen_inf}), so
1404	  \(V_0 \cap V_1 = \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\). Make \(N\) an algebra over the Laurent
1405	  polynomial ring via the composite
1406	  \[
1407	    k[T, T^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{01}^{-1}\ } \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1)
1408	      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma\bigl(X, \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1)\bigr) = N
1409	  \]
1410	  (\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}). This structure is compatible with the \(k\)-module
1411	  structure of \(N\): a scalar \(r \in k[T,T^{-1}]\) corresponds under \(\gamma_{01}\) to
1412	  the image of \(r\) under the algebra map into the overlap ring
1413	  (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(3)), which is the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\)
1414	  on \(U_0 \cap U_1\) (\ref{lem:P1_structureMap_appTop_awayToSection}), and \(\pi\) pulls
1415	  the structure algebra map of \(\PP^1\) back to that of \(X\)
1416	  (\ref{lem:appLE_overAlgebraMap}). Hence the \(k\)-module structure of \(N\) is the
1417	  restriction of scalars of the \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-structure along the canonical map
1418	  \(k \to k[T,T^{-1}]\).
1419	
1420	  (c) \emph{Module-finiteness over the Laurent ring.} Since \(\pi\) is finite and
1421	  \(U_0 \cap U_1\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\), the map
1422	  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \to N\) is module-finite
1423	  (\ref{lem:finite_app_overlap}); composing with the isomorphism \(\gamma_{01}^{-1}\),
1424	  \(N\) is a finite \(k[T,T^{-1}]\)-module.
1425	
1426	  (d) \emph{The two lattices, and the range of the difference map.} Let
1427	  \(Q_0, Q_1 \subseteq N\) be the images of the (\(k\)-linear) restriction maps
1428	  \(\Gamma(X, V_0) \to N\) and \(\Gamma(X, V_1) \to N\). Then
1429	  \(\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}) = Q_0 + Q_1\): every value
1430	  \(s_0| - s_1|\) of \(\mathrm{diff}\) is the sum of \(s_0| \in Q_0\) and
1431	  \(-(s_1|) = (-s_1)| \in Q_1\); conversely \(s_0| = \mathrm{diff}(s_0, 0) \) and
1432	  \(s_1| = \mathrm{diff}(0, -s_1)\) exhibit every element of \(Q_0\) and of \(Q_1\) as a
1433	  value of \(\mathrm{diff}\) --- the sign is absorbed because \(Q_1\) is the image of a
1434	  linear map.
1435	
1436	  (e) \emph{Lattice stability.} Let
1437	  \(\tau_0 = \pi^\sharp(t_{01}) \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) and
1438	  \(\tau_1 = \pi^\sharp(t_{10}) \in \Gamma(X, V_1)\) be the pullbacks of the chart
1439	  coordinates, regarded as sections over the charts
1440	  (Definition~\ref{def:P1_chartCoord}). By \ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(1) and the
1441	  compatibility of \(\pi^\sharp\) with restriction, \(T\) acts on \(N\) as
1442	  multiplication by \(\tau_0|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\); symmetrically \(T^{-1}\) acts as
1443	  multiplication by \(\tau_1|_{V_0 \cap V_1}\) (\ref{lem:P1_laurent_generators}(2)).
1444	  Hence \(Q_0\) is stable under multiplication by \(T\): for \(s \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\),
1445	  \[
1446	    T \cdot s|_{V_0 \cap V_1} \;=\; \tau_0|\cdot s| \;=\; (\tau_0 s)|_{V_0 \cap V_1}
1447	      \;\in\; Q_0,
1448	  \]
1449	  and symmetrically \(Q_1\) is stable under multiplication by \(T^{-1}\).
1450	
1451	  (f) \emph{Absorption up to powers.} The overlap is a basic open inside each chart
1452	  preimage: pulling back the identity \(D(t_{ij}) = U_i \cap U_j\) of
1453	  \ref{thm:P1_basicOpen_chartCoord} along \(\pi\) (basic opens of sections pull back to
1454	  basic opens of the pulled-back sections) gives
1455	  \[
1456	    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_0) \subseteq V_0,
1457	    \qquad
1458	    V_0 \cap V_1 = D(\tau_1) \subseteq V_1 .
1459	  \]
1460	  Since \(V_0\) is affine and \(V_0 \cap V_1\) is its basic open defined by \(\tau_0\),
1461	  restriction identifies \(N\) with the localization of \(\Gamma(X, V_0)\) at the powers
1462	  of \(\tau_0\) (quasi-coherence of the structure sheaf). Hence for every \(n \in N\)
1463	  there are \(m \ge 0\) and \(a \in \Gamma(X, V_0)\) with
1464	  \(n \cdot (\tau_0|)^m = a|\), i.e.\ \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\). Symmetrically, every
1465	  \(n \in N\) satisfies \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\) for some \(m \ge 0\).
1466	
1467	  (g) \emph{The ladder.} By (b), (c), (e) and (f), the module \(N\) over
1468	  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\) with the \(k\)-submodules \(Q_0, Q_1\) satisfies all hypotheses of the
1469	  two-lattice finiteness theorem in its localization form via powers of the generator
1470	  (\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc_pow}); hence \(N/(Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module. By
1471	  (d) this quotient is \(N/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff})\), and by (a) it is
1472	  \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\).
1473	\end{proof}
1474	
1475	\begin{theorem}[Finiteness of \(H^1\) of the curve]
1476	  \label{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
1477	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one}
1478	  \uses{def:HModule, def:moduleKSheaf}
1479	  \leanok
1480	  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth curve over \(k\) (proper, smooth of relative
1481	  dimension one, geometrically irreducible). Then
1482	  \(H^1\bigl(C, \struct{C/k}\bigr)\) is a finite \(k\)-module; equivalently, it is a
1483	  finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space.
1484	\end{theorem}
1485	\begin{proof}
1486	  \leanok
1487	  \uses{thm:exists_finite_toP1, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}
1488	  By \ref{thm:exists_finite_toP1} there is a finite morphism \(\pi : C \to \PP^1\) over
1489	  \(k\); apply \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1}.
1490	\end{proof}
1491	
1492	\begin{remark}[The genus is the dimension of a finite-dimensional space]
1493	  \label{rem:genus_finite}
1494	  \uses{def:genus, thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one}
1495	  \leanok
1496	  For a smooth curve \(C\) over \(k\), the genus of Definition~\ref{def:genus} is the
1497	  \(k\)-dimension of \(H^1(C, \struct C)\), which by
1498	  \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one} is a finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space; the
1499	  genus is therefore a well-defined natural number, attained as the cardinality of any
1500	  basis.

5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.TwoLattice
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FinitenessP1
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1
9	
10	/-!
11	# Finiteness of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` via a finite morphism to the projective line
12	
13	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` equipped with a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, this
14	file proves that the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf of `X` (as a sheaf of
15	`k`-modules on the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) is a finite `k`-module — and derives
16	the instance for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of the challenge, so that
17	`genus` is the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional vector space.
18	
19	The proof is the *two-lattice ladder* of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.TwoLattice` run on the
20	Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover`:
21	
22	* `V i := π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` is an affine open cover of `X`
23	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), so
24	  `H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁) ⧸ range (res₀ - res₁)` (`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`);
25	* `N := Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` is a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]` through
26	  `π`'s map on sections over the chart overlap and the identification
27	  `Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(X₀X₁)) ≃ k[T,T⁻¹]` (`P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`); it is module-finite because `π`
28	  is finite (`finite_app_overlap`);
29	* `Q₀, Q₁ :=` the images of `Γ(V₀), Γ(V₁)` in `N` are `k`-submodules with
30	  `range (res₀ - res₁) = Q₀ ⊔ Q₁`; `Q₀` is stable under `T` because `T` is the restriction
31	  of the chart-0 coordinate, which extends to `V₀` (symmetrically for `Q₁` and `T⁻¹`); and
32	  `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate inside the affine `V₀`
33	  (`P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`), so
34	  `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen` provides the surjectivity-up-to-powers
35	  hypotheses of the two-lattice lemma.
36	
37	The `ℙ¹`-side identifications live in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FinitenessP1`.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` — **the conditional
42	  finiteness theorem**: if `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹` is finite with `π ≫ P1.structureMap k = X ↘ Spec k`,
43	  then `Module.Finite k (H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪_X))`.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one` — the instance for the challenge curve
45	  `C` (smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over `k`), consuming
46	  `exists_isFinite_toP1`; it is keyed on exactly the `letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k))`
47	  spelling used by `genus` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.
48	
49	`FiniteDimensional k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` is *definitionally* the statement of the instance
50	(`FiniteDimensional` is an abbreviation for `Module.Finite`), so no separate corollary is
51	needed.
52	-/

80	private lemma preimage_overlap_eq :
81	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 =
82	      π ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) := by
83	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf, P1.chartOpen_inf k]

85	private lemma preimage_overlap_le :
86	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 ≤
87	      π ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) :=
88	  (preimage_overlap_eq π).le

90	/-- The `k[T;T⁻¹]`-algebra structure map on the sections of the chart-preimage overlap:
91	`π`'s map on sections over `D₊(X₀X₁)` composed with the Laurent identification. Only used
92	as a local `Algebra` instance inside the finiteness argument. -/
93	private noncomputable def overlapLaurentHom :
94	    LaurentPolynomial k →+* Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) :=
95	  ((π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom).comp
96	    (P1.overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm.toRingHom
97	
98	/-- `T` acts on the overlap sections as multiplication by the restriction of the
99	pulled-back chart-0 coordinate, which extends to `π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(X₀)`. -/
100	private lemma overlapLaurentHom_T_one :
101	    overlapLaurentHom π (LaurentPolynomial.T 1) =
102	      (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : _ ⊓ _ ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0)).op).hom
103	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
104	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1))) := by
105	  change (π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
106	      ((P1.overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T 1)) = _
107	  rw [P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T]
108	  calc (π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
109	        (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_left k)).op).hom
110	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)))
111	      = ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_left k)).op ≫
112	          π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
113	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)) := rfl
114	    _ = (π.appLE (P1.chartOpen k 0) _ ((preimage_overlap_le π).trans
115	          ((Opens.map π.base).map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_left k))).le)).hom
116	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
117	        rw [Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
118	    _ = (π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0) ≫
119	          Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : _ ⊓ _ ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0)).op).hom
120	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)) := by
121	        rw [Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
122	    _ = _ := rfl

124	/-- `T⁻¹` acts on the overlap sections as multiplication by the restriction of the
125	pulled-back chart-1 coordinate, which extends to `π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(X₁)`. -/
126	private lemma overlapLaurentHom_T_neg_one :
127	    overlapLaurentHom π (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1)) =
128	      (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : _ ⊓ _ ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)).op).hom
129	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
130	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0))) := by
131	  change (π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
132	      ((P1.overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1))) = _
133	  rw [P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_T_neg]
134	  calc (π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
135	        (((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_right k)).op).hom
136	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)))
137	      = ((P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_right k)).op ≫
138	          π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
139	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)) := rfl
140	    _ = (π.appLE (P1.chartOpen k 1) _ ((preimage_overlap_le π).trans
141	          ((Opens.map π.base).map (homOfLE (P1.overlap_le_right k))).le)).hom
142	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
143	        rw [Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
144	    _ = (π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1) ≫
145	          Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : _ ⊓ _ ≤ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)).op).hom
146	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)) := by
147	        rw [Scheme.Hom.app_eq_appLE, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
148	    _ = _ := rfl

150	/-- The Laurent algebra structure map is compatible with the structure algebra map of `Y`
151	over `k`. This is the input for the `IsScalarTower k k[T;T⁻¹] Γ(Y, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` instance. -/
152	private lemma overlapLaurentHom_algebraMap [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
153	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) (r : k) :
154	    overlapLaurentHom π (algebraMap k (LaurentPolynomial k) r) =
155	      Y.overAlgebraMap k (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) r := by
156	  letI : (P1 k).Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨P1.structureMap k⟩
157	  have hcomp : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv ≫ (P1.structureMap k).appTop ≫
158	      (P1 k).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) ≤ ⊤)).op =
159	      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1))) ≫
160	        Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1) := by
161	    rw [P1.structureMap_appTop_awayToSection k (P1.X_mul_X_mem k) two_pos,
162	      Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
163	  have hPA : (P1 k).overAlgebraMap k (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) r =
164	      (Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)).hom (algebraMap k (Away 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) r) :=
165	    congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom $hcomp) r)
166	  have hLHS := π.appLE_overAlgebraMap hπ (preimage_overlap_le π) r
167	  change (π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _ (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom
168	      ((P1.overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm (algebraMap k (LaurentPolynomial k) r)) = _
169	  rw [P1.overlapSectionsEquiv_symm_algebraMap, ← hPA]
170	  exact hLHS
