172	/-- The chart-preimage overlap is the basic open of the pulled-back chart-0 coordinate. -/
173	private lemma preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_left :
174	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 =
175	      Y.basicOpen ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
176	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1))) := by
177	  have h : π ⁻¹ᵁ ((P1 k).basicOpen
178	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1))) =
179	      Y.basicOpen ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
180	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1))) :=
181	    Scheme.preimage_basicOpen π _
182	  rw [P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord k 0 1, Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf] at h
183	  exact h
184	
185	/-- The chart-preimage overlap is the basic open of the pulled-back chart-1 coordinate. -/
186	private lemma preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_right :
187	    π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 =
188	      Y.basicOpen ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
189	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0))) := by
190	  have h : π ⁻¹ᵁ ((P1 k).basicOpen
191	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0))) =
192	      Y.basicOpen ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
193	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0))) :=
194	    Scheme.preimage_basicOpen π _
195	  rw [P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord k 1 0, Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf] at h
196	  rw [← h, inf_comm]

201	/-- The `k`-linear restriction map `Γ(Y, U₀) →ₗ[k] Γ(Y, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`, with the
202	`Scheme.overModule` structures (the left leg of the Mayer–Vietoris difference map). -/
203	private noncomputable def resLeft [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] :
204	    Γ(Y, U₀) →ₗ[k] Γ(Y, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
205	  ((Y.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₀)).op).hom
206	
207	variable (k) in
208	/-- The `k`-linear restriction map `Γ(Y, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(Y, U₀ ⊓ U₁)`, with the
209	`Scheme.overModule` structures (the right leg of the Mayer–Vietoris difference map). -/
210	private noncomputable def resRight [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] :
211	    Γ(Y, U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(Y, U₀ ⊓ U₁) :=
212	  ((Y.moduleKSheaf k).obj.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U₀ ⊓ U₁ ≤ U₁)).op).hom
213	
214	variable {U₀ U₁} in
215	/-- The restriction-difference map of the two-cover has range `Q₀ ⊔ Q₁`, the join of the
216	images of the two restriction maps. -/
217	private lemma range_diff_eq [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] :
218	    LinearMap.range (TwoCover.diff k Y U₀ U₁) =
219	      LinearMap.range (resLeft k (Y := Y) U₀ U₁) ⊔
220	        LinearMap.range (resRight k (Y := Y) U₀ U₁) := by
221	  refine le_antisymm ?_ (sup_le ?_ ?_)
222	  · rintro x ⟨t, rfl⟩
223	    rw [TwoCover.diff_apply]
224	    exact Submodule.sub_mem _ (Submodule.mem_sup_left ⟨t.1, rfl⟩)
225	      (Submodule.mem_sup_right ⟨t.2, rfl⟩)
226	  · rintro x ⟨s, rfl⟩
227	    refine ⟨(s, 0), ?_⟩
228	    rw [TwoCover.diff_apply]
229	    change Y.resHom inf_le_left s - Y.resHom inf_le_right 0 = Y.resHom inf_le_left s
230	    rw [map_zero, sub_zero]
231	  · rintro x ⟨s, rfl⟩
232	    refine ⟨(0, -s), ?_⟩
233	    rw [TwoCover.diff_apply]
234	    change Y.resHom inf_le_left 0 - Y.resHom inf_le_right (-s) = Y.resHom inf_le_right s
235	    rw [map_zero, map_neg, zero_sub, neg_neg]
236	
237	/-- **The two-lattice ladder on the chart-preimage cover**: for a finite `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` over
238	`Spec k`, the Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of the affine cover `π⁻¹D₊(X₀), π⁻¹D₊(X₁)` is a
239	finite `k`-module. -/
240	private theorem moduleFinite_h1Cok [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsFinite π]
241	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) :
242	    Module.Finite k
243	      (TwoCover.H1Cok k Y (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)) := by
244	  classical
245	  have hV₀ : IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0
246	  have hV₁ : IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) := isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1
247	  -- the Laurent module structure on the overlap sections
248	  letI : Algebra (LaurentPolynomial k)
249	      Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) :=
250	    (overlapLaurentHom π).toAlgebra
251	  -- the compatible `k`-structure
252	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (LaurentPolynomial k)
253	      Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) := by
254	    refine ⟨fun a b n => ?_⟩
255	    rw [Algebra.smul_def ((a • b : LaurentPolynomial k)) n, Algebra.smul_def b n,
256	      Scheme.overModule_smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, Algebra.smul_def a b,
257	      map_mul, overlapLaurentHom_algebraMap π hπ, mul_assoc]
258	  -- module-finiteness over the Laurent polynomials, from finiteness of `π`
259	  haveI : Module.Finite (LaurentPolynomial k)
260	      Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) := by
261	    have h1 : ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (preimage_overlap_le π)).op).hom).Finite := by
262	      refine RingHom.Finite.of_surjective _ ?_
263	      rw [show homOfLE (preimage_overlap_le π) = eqToHom (preimage_overlap_eq π) from
264	        Subsingleton.elim _ _]
265	      exact ((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
266	        (Y.presheaf.map (eqToHom (preimage_overlap_eq π)).op)).mp inferInstance).2
267	    have h2 : ((π.appLE (Proj.basicOpen 𝒜 (X 0 * X 1)) _
268	        (preimage_overlap_le π)).hom).Finite :=
269	      h1.comp (finite_app_overlap π)
270	    exact h2.comp (P1.overlapSectionsEquiv k).symm.finite
271	  -- `Q₀` is stable under `T`
272	  have hstab₀ : ∀ x ∈ LinearMap.range (resLeft k (Y := Y)
273	        (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)),
274	      (LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) • x ∈
275	        LinearMap.range (resLeft k (Y := Y)
276	          (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)) := by
277	    rintro x ⟨s, rfl⟩
278	    refine ⟨(π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
279	      ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)) * s, ?_⟩
280	    change (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom
281	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
282	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)) * s) = _
283	    rw [map_mul, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, overlapLaurentHom_T_one]
284	    rfl
285	  -- `Q₁` is stable under `T⁻¹`
286	  have hstab₁ : ∀ x ∈ LinearMap.range (resRight k (Y := Y)
287	        (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)),
288	      (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) • x ∈
289	        LinearMap.range (resRight k (Y := Y)
290	          (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)) := by
291	    rintro x ⟨s, rfl⟩
292	    refine ⟨(π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
293	      ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)) * s, ?_⟩
294	    change (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom
295	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
296	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)) * s) = _
297	    rw [map_mul, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra,
298	      overlapLaurentHom_T_neg_one]
299	    rfl
300	  -- surjectivity up to powers of `T` towards `Q₀`
301	  have hloc₀ : ∀ n : Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1),
302	      ∃ m : ℕ, ((LaurentPolynomial.T 1 : LaurentPolynomial k) ^ m) • n ∈
303	        LinearMap.range (resLeft k (Y := Y)
304	          (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)) := by
305	    intro n
306	    have key : ∃ (m : ℕ) (a : Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0)),
307	        n * ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom
308	            ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
309	              ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)))) ^ m =
310	          (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom a := by
311	      letI : Algebra Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0)
312	          Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) :=
313	        ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom).toAlgebra
314	      haveI := hV₀.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen
315	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
316	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1)))
317	        (homOfLE inf_le_left) (preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_left π)
318	      obtain ⟨m, a, ha⟩ := IsLocalization.Away.surj
319	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 0)).hom
320	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 0 1))) n
321	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra] at ha
322	      exact ⟨m, a, ha⟩
323	    obtain ⟨m, a, ha⟩ := key
324	    refine ⟨m, a, ?_⟩
325	    change (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom a = _
326	    rw [Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, map_pow, overlapLaurentHom_T_one,
327	      ← ha, mul_comm]
328	  -- surjectivity up to powers of `T⁻¹` towards `Q₁`
329	  have hloc₁ : ∀ n : Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1),
330	      ∃ m : ℕ, ((LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) : LaurentPolynomial k) ^ m) • n ∈
331	        LinearMap.range (resRight k (Y := Y)
332	          (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)) := by
333	    intro n
334	    have key : ∃ (m : ℕ) (a : Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)),
335	        n * ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom
336	            ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
337	              ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)))) ^ m =
338	          (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom a := by
339	      letI : Algebra Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)
340	          Γ(Y, π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊓ π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1) :=
341	        ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom).toAlgebra
342	      haveI := hV₁.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen
343	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
344	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0)))
345	        (homOfLE inf_le_right) (preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_right π)
346	      obtain ⟨m, a, ha⟩ := IsLocalization.Away.surj
347	        ((π.app (P1.chartOpen k 1)).hom
348	          ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 1)).hom (P1.chartCoord k 1 0))) n
349	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra] at ha
350	      exact ⟨m, a, ha⟩
351	    obtain ⟨m, a, ha⟩ := key
352	    refine ⟨m, a, ?_⟩
353	    change (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom a = _
354	    rw [Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, map_pow,
355	      overlapLaurentHom_T_neg_one, ← ha, mul_comm]
356	  -- run the two-lattice ladder and transport to the cokernel
357	  haveI hquot := LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_exists_pow_smul_mem
358	    hstab₀ hstab₁ hloc₀ hloc₁
359	  exact Module.Finite.equiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _
360	    (range_diff_eq (U₀ := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 0) (U₁ := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1)).symm)
361

19	This file defines the Picard group `CommRing.Pic R` of a commutative ring `R` as the type of
20	invertible `R`-modules (in the sense that `M` is invertible if there exists another `R`-module
21	`N` such that `M ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[R] R`) up to isomorphism, equipped with tensor product as multiplication.

24

634	private theorem projective_units_and_mul'_comp_lTensor_bijective (I : (Submodule R A)ˣ) :
635	    Projective R I ∧ Function.Bijective (mul' R A ∘ₗ I.1.subtype.lTensor A) := by
636	  obtain ⟨T, T', hT, hT', one_mem⟩ := mem_span_mul_finite_of_mem_mul (I.inv_mul ▸ one_le.mp le_rfl)
637	  classical
638	  rw [← Set.image2_mul, ← Finset.coe_image₂, mem_span_finset] at one_mem
639	  set S := T.image₂ (· * ·) T'
640	  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := one_mem
641	  choose a ha b hb eq using fun i : S ↦ Finset.mem_image₂.mp i.2
642	  let f : I →ₗ[R] S → R := .pi fun i ↦ (LinearEquiv.ofInjective
643	      (Algebra.linearMap R A) (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R A)).symm.comp <|
644	    restrict (mulRight R (r i • a i)) fun x hx ↦ by
645	      rw [← one_eq_range, ← I.mul_inv]; exact mul_mem_mul hx (I⁻¹.1.smul_mem _ <| hT <| ha i)
646	  have hf (x : I.1) (i : S) : algebraMap R A (f x i) = x * r i • a i := by
647	    dsimp [f, ← Algebra.linearMap_apply]
648	    exact LinearEquiv.ofInjective_symm_apply ..
649	  let g : (S → R) →ₗ[R] I := .lsum _ _ ℕ fun i ↦ .toSpanSingleton _ _ ⟨b i, hT' <| hb i⟩
650	  have hgf : g ∘ₗ f = .id := LinearMap.ext fun x ↦ Subtype.ext <| by
651	    simp only [g, lsum_apply, comp_apply, sum_apply, toSpanSingleton_apply, proj_apply]
652	    simp_rw [coe_sum, coe_smul, Algebra.smul_def, hf, mul_assoc, ← Finset.mul_sum,
653	      Algebra.smul_mul_assoc, eq, (Finset.sum_coe_sort ..).trans hr.2, mul_one, id_apply]
654	  set m := mul' R A ∘ₗ I.1.subtype.lTensor A
655	  have eq : (piScalarRight R R A S).toLinearMap ∘ₗ f.lTensor A =
656	      (.pi fun i : S ↦ mulRight R (r i • a i)) ∘ₗ m := by
657	    ext; simp [(Algebra.smul_def ..).trans (Algebra.commutes ..), hf, m, mul_assoc]
658	  have := (piScalarRight R R A S).injective.comp <| injective_of_comp_eq_id
659	    (f.lTensor A) (g.lTensor A) <| by rw [← lTensor_comp, hgf, lTensor_id]
660	  rw [← LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap, ← coe_comp, eq, coe_comp] at this
661	  refine ⟨.of_split f g hgf, .of_comp this, range_eq_top.mp ?_⟩
662	  rw [show m = mulMap ⊤ I ∘ₗ (topEquiv.symm.rTensor I.1).toLinearMap by ext; rfl, range_comp,
663	    LinearEquiv.range, map_top, mulMap_range, top_mul_eq_top_of_mul_eq_one I.inv_mul]

678	noncomputable def tensorEquivMul : I ⊗[R] J ≃ₗ[R] I * J := by

698	the Picard group of `R`. See Lemma 2.2 in [RobertsSingh1993]. -/
699	@[simps] noncomputable def unitsToPic : (Submodule R A)ˣ →* Pic R where
700	  toFun I := Pic.mk R I

702	    ⟨.ofEq _ _ one_eq_range ≪≫ₗ .symm (.ofInjective _ (FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective R A))⟩
703	  map_mul' I J := by rw [← mk_tensor, mk_eq_mk_iff]; exact ⟨(tensorEquivMul I J).symm⟩

706	noncomputable def unitsToPicEquiv (I : (Submodule R A)ˣ) : unitsToPic R A I ≃ₗ[R] I :=

711	theorem ker_unitsToPic :
712	    (unitsToPic R A).ker = (Units.map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom).range := by
713	  ext I; constructor <;> intro h
714	  · have e := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp h).some.symm
715	    have e' := (mk_eq_one_iff.mp (inv_mem h)).some.symm
716	    have h := eq_span_singleton_of_surjective e.surjective
717	    have h' := eq_span_singleton_of_surjective e'.surjective
718	    refine ⟨(isUnit_iff_exists_and_exists.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩).unit, Units.ext h.symm⟩
719	    · have : span R {(e 1).1 * e' 1} = 1 := by simpa [span_mul_span] using congr($h * $h').symm
720	      have ⟨r, hr⟩ := span_singleton_eq_one_iff.mp this
721	      exact ⟨e' 1 * algebraMap R A r.inv, by simp [← mul_assoc, hr, ← map_mul]⟩
722	    · have : span R {(e' 1).1 * e 1} = 1 := by simpa [span_mul_span] using congr($h' * $h).symm
723	      have ⟨r, hr⟩ := span_singleton_eq_one_iff.mp this
724	      exact ⟨algebraMap R A r.inv * e' 1, by simp [mul_assoc, hr, ← map_mul]⟩
725	  · obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := h
726	    exact mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨.symm <| (.ofInjective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton R A x) fun _ _ eq ↦
727	      (faithfulSMul_iff_injective_smul_one R A).mp ‹_› <| by simpa using congr($eq * x.inv)) ≪≫ₗ
728	      .ofEq _ _ (by ext; simp [mem_span_singleton])⟩

731	at `(Submodule R A)ˣ`. -/

733	    Function.MulExact (Units.map (spanSingleton R).toMonoidHom) (unitsToPic R A) :=
734	  MonoidHom.mulExact_iff.mpr (ker_unitsToPic R A)

818	    exact mk_eq_one_iff.mpr ⟨AlgebraTensorModule.congr (.refl ..) (unitsToPicEquiv I) ≪≫ₗ

827	    (mk_eq_one_iff.mp <| by simp_rw [mk_tensor, mk_eq_self, mul_inv_cancel]).some).symm ≪≫ₗ

832	  obtain ⟨a, -, eq⟩ := mem_mul_span_singleton.mp (this ▸ mem_top (x := 1))

875	  have ⟨I, eq⟩ := Submodule.range_unitsToPic R (FractionRing R) ▸ this

877	  ⟨_, ⟨e ≪≫ₗ FractionalIdeal.equivNumOfIsLocalization

890	/-- In a total ring of fractions, if two ideals are inverse to each other in the Picard group,
891	the only possibility is that they are both the whole ring. -/
892	theorem Ideal.eq_top_of_mk_tensor_eq_one [IsFractionRing R R] (I J : Ideal R)
893	    [Module.Invertible R I] [Module.Invertible R J] (h : Pic.mk R (I ⊗[R] J) = 1) :
894	    I = ⊤ ∧ J = ⊤ := by
895	  have ⟨e⟩ := mk_eq_one_iff.mp h
896	  have e := e.symm ≪≫ₗ Submodule.LinearDisjoint.mulMap
897	    (.of_left_le_one_of_flat I J <| le_top.trans one_eq_top.ge)
898	  have : IsUnit (e 1 : R) := IsFractionRing.self_iff_nonZeroDivisors_le_isUnit.mp ‹_› <|
899	      IsRegular.mem_nonZeroDivisors <| isRightRegular_iff_isRegular.mp <| by

/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Andrew Yang
-/
module

public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Limits
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Over.Pullback
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Constructions.Over.Products
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.CommMon_
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Grp
public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Pullback.IsPullback.Basic

/-!

# `CartesianMonoidalCategory` for `Over X`

We provide a `CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance via pullbacks, and provide simp lemmas
for the induced `MonoidalCategory (Over X)` instance.

-/

public noncomputable section

namespace CategoryTheory.Over

open Functor Limits CartesianMonoidalCategory

variable {C : Type*} [Category* C] [HasPullbacks C]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
/-- A choice of finite products of `Over X` given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev cartesianMonoidalCategory (X : C) : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofChosenFiniteProducts
    ⟨asEmptyCone (Over.mk (𝟙 X)), IsTerminal.ofUniqueHom (fun Y ↦ Over.homMk Y.hom)
      fun Y m ↦ Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simpa using m.w)⟩
    fun Y Z ↦ ⟨pullbackConeEquivBinaryFan.functor.obj (pullback.cone Y.hom Z.hom),
    (pullback.isLimit _ _).pullbackConeEquivBinaryFanFunctor⟩

attribute [local instance] cartesianMonoidalCategory

/-- `Over X` is braided w.r.t. the Cartesian monoidal structure given by `Limits.pullback`. -/
abbrev braidedCategory (X : C) : BraidedCategory (Over X) :=
  .ofCartesianMonoidalCategory

attribute [local instance] braidedCategory

open MonoidalCategory

variable {X : C}

@[ext]
lemma tensorObj_ext {R : C} {S T : Over X} (f₁ f₂ : R ⟶ (S ⊗ T).left)
    (e₁ : f₁ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.fst _ _)
    (e₂ : f₁ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = f₂ ≫ pullback.snd _ _) : f₁ = f₂ :=
  pullback.hom_ext e₁ e₂

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_left (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).left = Limits.pullback R.hom S.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorObj_hom (R S : Over X) : (R ⊗ S).hom = pullback.fst R.hom S.hom ≫ R.hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_left : (𝟙_ (Over X)).left = X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma tensorUnit_hom : (𝟙_ (Over X)).hom = 𝟙 X := rfl

@[simp]
lemma lift_left {R S T : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : R ⟶ T) :
    (lift f g).left = pullback.lift f.left g.left (f.w.trans g.w.symm) := rfl

@[simp]
lemma fst_left {R S : Over X} : (fst R S).left = pullback.fst _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma snd_left {R S : Over X} : (snd R S).left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma toUnit_left {R : Over X} : (toUnit R).left = R.hom := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_hom_left_snd_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).hom.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_fst (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
      pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_fst_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π_assoc _ _ _).trans (limit.lift_π _ _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma associator_inv_left_snd (R S T : Over X) :
    (α_ R S T).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ _) _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma leftUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.snd _ _ := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst (𝟙 X) _ = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma leftUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (λ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd (𝟙 X) _ = 𝟙 Y.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma rightUnitor_hom_left (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).hom.left = pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 _ :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (𝟙 X) = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerLeft_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) f.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerLeft_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (R ◁ f).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

lemma whiskerRight_left {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerRight_left_fst {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma whiskerRight_left_snd {R S T : Over X} (f : S ⟶ T) :
    (f ▷ R).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ :=
  (limit.lift_π _ _).trans (Category.comp_id _)

lemma tensorHom_left {R S T U : Over X} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ U) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left = pullback.map _ _ _ _ f.left g.left (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp) := rfl

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma tensorHom_left_fst {S U : C} {R T : Over X} (fS : S ⟶ X) (fU : U ⟶ X)
    (f : R ⟶ mk fS) (g : T ⟶ mk fU) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left ≫ pullback.fst fS fU = pullback.fst R.hom T.hom ≫ f.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma tensorHom_left_snd {S U : C} {R T : Over X} (fS : S ⟶ X) (fU : U ⟶ X)
    (f : R ⟶ mk fS) (g : T ⟶ mk fU) :
    (f ⊗ₘ g).left ≫ pullback.snd fS fU = pullback.snd R.hom T.hom ≫ g.left :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

@[simp]
lemma braiding_hom_left {R S : Over X} :
    (β_ R S).hom.left = (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom := rfl

@[simp]
lemma braiding_inv_left {R S : Over X} :
    (β_ R S).inv.left = (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom := rfl

variable {A B R S Y Z : C} {f : R ⟶ X} {g : S ⟶ X}

instance : (Over.pullback f).Braided := .ofChosenFiniteProducts _

@[simp]
lemma η_pullback_left : (OplaxMonoidal.η (Over.pullback f)).left = (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f) := rfl

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma ε_pullback_left : (LaxMonoidal.ε (Over.pullback f)).left = inv (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f) := by
  apply IsIso.eq_inv_of_hom_inv_id
  rw [← η_pullback_left, ← Over.comp_left, Monoidal.η_ε, Over.id_left]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_fst (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left, ← Over.comp_left_assoc,
    Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, fst]

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_snd (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫
      pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left,
    ← Over.comp_left_assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, snd]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma μ_pullback_left_snd (R S : Over X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) R S).left ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ := by
  rw [Monoidal.μ_of_cartesianMonoidalCategory,
    ← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) R S).hom.left,
    ← Over.comp_left_assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison]

@[simp]
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_fst' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f ≫ pullback.fst g₁ g₂ =
        pullback.fst _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  μ_pullback_left_fst_fst ..

@[simp]
lemma μ_pullback_left_fst_snd' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f ≫ pullback.snd g₁ g₂ =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  μ_pullback_left_fst_snd ..

@[simp]
lemma μ_pullback_left_snd' (g₁ : Y ⟶ X) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X) :
    (LaxMonoidal.μ (Over.pullback f) (.mk g₁) (.mk g₂)).left ≫
      pullback.snd (pullback.fst g₁ g₂ ≫ g₁) f =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ := μ_pullback_left_snd ..

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma preservesTerminalIso_pullback (f : R ⟶ S) :
    preservesTerminalIso (Over.pullback f) =
      Over.isoMk (asIso (pullback.snd (𝟙 _) f)) (by simp) := by
  ext1; exact toUnit_unique _ _

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_fst_fst (f : X ⟶ Y) (A B : Over Y) :
    (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) A B).inv.left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst A.hom B.hom ≫ A.hom) f ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
        pullback.fst (pullback.snd A.hom f) (pullback.snd B.hom f) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) A B).hom.left,
    Over.hom_left_inv_left_assoc]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, fst]

@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_Spec_inv_left_fst_fst' (f : X ⟶ Y) (gA : A ⟶ Y) (gB : B ⟶ Y) :
    (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) (.mk gA) (.mk gB)).inv.left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst gA gB ≫ gA) f ≫ pullback.fst _ _ =
        pullback.fst (pullback.snd gA f) (pullback.snd gB f) ≫ pullback.fst _ _ :=
  prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_fst_fst ..

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_fst_snd' (f : X ⟶ Y) (gA : A ⟶ Y) (gB : B ⟶ Y) :
    (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) (.mk gA) (.mk gB)).inv.left ≫
      pullback.fst (pullback.fst gA gB ≫ gA) f ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
        pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) _ _).hom.left,
    Over.hom_left_inv_left_assoc]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison, snd]

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
lemma prodComparisonIso_pullback_inv_left_snd' (f : X ⟶ Y) (gA : A ⟶ Y) (gB : B ⟶ Y) :
    (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) (.mk gA) (.mk gB)).inv.left ≫
      pullback.snd (pullback.fst gA gB ≫ gA) f = pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _ := by
  rw [← cancel_epi (prodComparisonIso (Over.pullback f) _ _).hom.left,
    Over.hom_left_inv_left_assoc]
  simp [CartesianMonoidalCategory.prodComparison]

/-- The pullback of a monoid object is a monoid object. -/
@[simps! -isSimp mul one]
abbrev monObjMkPullbackSnd [MonObj (Over.mk f)] : MonObj (Over.mk <| pullback.snd f g) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapMon.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).mon

attribute [local instance] monObjMkPullbackSnd

instance isCommMonObj_mk_pullbackSnd [MonObj (Over.mk f)] [IsCommMonObj (Over.mk f)] :
    IsCommMonObj (Over.mk <| pullback.snd f g) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapCommMon.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).comm

/-- The pullback of a monoid object is a monoid object. -/
@[simps! -isSimp mul one]
abbrev grpObjMkPullbackSnd [GrpObj (Over.mk f)] : GrpObj (Over.mk (pullback.snd f g)) :=
  ((Over.pullback g).mapGrp.obj <| .mk <| .mk f).grp

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
attribute [local simp] monObjMkPullbackSnd_one in
instance isMonHom_pullbackFst_id_right [MonObj (Over.mk f)] :
    IsMonHom <| Over.homMk (U := Over.mk <| pullback.snd f (𝟙 X)) (V := Over.mk f)
      (pullback.fst f (𝟙 X)) (pullback.condition.trans <| by simp) where

    dsimp [monObjMkPullbackSnd_mul]

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: Christian Merten
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
11	
12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
20	
21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
22	over a field, proper over that field.
23	
24	## Main definitions
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
31	
32	## Main theorems
33	
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
41	
42	## Notes
43	
44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
47	-/
48	
49	set_option autoImplicit false
50	
51	universe u
52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
58	  -- smooth curve
59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
60	  -- proper
61	  [IsProper C.hom]
62	  -- geometrically irreducible
63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
73	
74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
75	
76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
82	  assoc := Category.assoc
83	
84	-- data
85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
93	
94	-- data
95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
99	  sorry
100	
101	namespace Jacobian
102	
103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
104	
105	-- data
106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
108	  sorry
109	
110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
111	genus of `C`. -/
112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
113	  sorry
114	
115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
117	  sorry
118	
119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
121	  sorry
122	
123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=

section CartesianMonoidalCategory

instance : CartesianMonoidalCategory (Over S) := Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory _
instance : BraidedCategory (Over S) := .ofCartesianMonoidalCategory

end CartesianMonoidalCategory

section Spec

variable (R S T : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T]

open TensorProduct Algebra.TensorProduct CommRingCat RingHomClass

/-- The isomorphism between the fibred product of two schemes `Spec S` and `Spec T`
over a scheme `Spec R` and the `Spec` of the tensor product `S ⊗[R] T`. -/
noncomputable
def pullbackSpecIso :
    pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R S)))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R T))) ≅ Spec (.of <| S ⊗[R] T) :=
  letI H := IsLimit.equivIsoLimit (PullbackCone.eta _)
    (PushoutCocone.isColimitEquivIsLimitOp _ (CommRingCat.pushoutCoconeIsColimit R S T))
  limit.isoLimitCone ⟨_, isLimitPullbackConeMapOfIsLimit Scheme.Spec _ H⟩

/--
The composition of the inverse of the isomorphism `pullbackSpecIso R S T` (from the pullback of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec R` and `Spec T ⟶ Spec R` to `Spec (S ⊗[R] T)`) with the first projection is
the morphism `Spec (S ⊗[R] T) ⟶ Spec S` obtained by applying `Spec.map` to the ring morphism
`s ↦ s ⊗ₜ[R] 1`.
-/
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).inv ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = Spec.map (ofHom includeLeftRingHom) :=
  limit.isoLimitCone_inv_π _ _

@[reassoc]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst' :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).inv ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap S _)) :=
  pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst ..

/--
The composition of the inverse of the isomorphism `pullbackSpecIso R S T` (from the pullback of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec R` and `Spec T ⟶ Spec R` to `Spec (S ⊗[R] T)`) with the second projection is
the morphism `Spec (S ⊗[R] T) ⟶ Spec T` obtained by applying `Spec.map` to the ring morphism
`t ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] t`.
-/
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).inv ≫ pullback.snd _ _ =
      Spec.map (ofHom (R := T) (S := S ⊗[R] T) (toRingHom includeRight)) :=
  limit.isoLimitCone_inv_π _ _

/--
The composition of the isomorphism `pullbackSpecIso R S T` (from the pullback of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec R` and `Spec T ⟶ Spec R` to `Spec (S ⊗[R] T)`) with the morphism
`Spec (S ⊗[R] T) ⟶ Spec S` obtained by applying `Spec.map` to the ring morphism `s ↦ s ⊗ₜ[R] 1`
is the first projection.
-/
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).hom ≫ Spec.map (ofHom includeLeftRingHom) = pullback.fst _ _ := by
  rw [← pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst' :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).hom ≫ Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap S _)) = pullback.fst _ _ :=
  pullbackSpecIso_hom_fst ..

/--
The composition of the isomorphism `pullbackSpecIso R S T` (from the pullback of
`Spec S ⟶ Spec R` and `Spec T ⟶ Spec R` to `Spec (S ⊗[R] T)`) with the morphism
`Spec (S ⊗[R] T) ⟶ Spec T` obtained by applying `Spec.map` to the ring morphism `t ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ[R] t`
is the second projection.
-/
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma pullbackSpecIso_hom_snd :
    (pullbackSpecIso R S T).hom ≫ Spec.map (ofHom (toRingHom includeRight)) = pullback.snd _ _ := by
  rw [← pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

9	\section*{5 The Cohomology of Projective Space}
10	
11	In this section we make explicit calculations of the cohomology of the
12	sheaves $\mathcal{O}(n)$ on a projective space, by using \v{C}ech cohomology
13	for a suitable open affine covering. These explicit calculations form the
14	basis for various general results about cohomology of coherent sheaves on
15	projective varieties.
16	
17	Let $A$ be a noetherian ring, let $S = A[x_0, \ldots, x_r]$, and let
18	$X = \Proj S$ be the projective space $\mathbf{P}^r_A$ over $A$. Let
19	$\mathcal{O}_X(1)$ be the twisting sheaf of Serre (II, \S 5). For any sheaf
20	of $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules $\mathcal{F}$, we denote by $\Gamma_*(\mathcal{F})$
21	the graded $S$-module $\bigoplus_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}(n))$
22	(see II, \S 5).
23	
24	\begin{theorem}[5.1]
25	Let $A$ be a noetherian ring, and let $X = \mathbf{P}^r_A$, with $r \ge 1$.
26	Then:
27	\begin{enumerate}
28	\item[(a)] the natural map $S \to \Gamma_*(\mathcal{O}_X) =
29	  \bigoplus_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n))$ is an isomorphism of
30	  graded $S$-modules;
31	\item[(b)] $H^i(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = 0$ for $0 < i < r$ and all
32	  $n \in \mathbf{Z}$;
33	\item[(c)] $H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-r-1)) \cong A$;
34	\item[(d)] the natural map
35	  \[
36	    H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) \times H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-n-r-1)) \to
37	    H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-r-1)) \cong A
38	  \]
39	  is a perfect pairing of finitely generated free $A$-modules, for each
40	  $n \in \mathbf{Z}$.
41	\end{enumerate}
42	\end{theorem}
43	
44	\begin{proof}
45	Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf
46	$\bigoplus_{n \in \mathbf{Z}} \mathcal{O}_X(n)$. Since cohomology commutes
47	with arbitrary direct sums on a noetherian topological space (2.9.1), the
48	cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$ will be the direct sum of the cohomology of the
49	sheaves $\mathcal{O}(n)$. So we will compute the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$,

11	of the grading by $n$, so that we can sort out the pieces at the end. Note
12	that all the cohomology groups in question have a natural structure of
13	$A$-module (2.6.1).
14	
15	For each $i = 0, \ldots, r$, let $U_i$ be the open set $D_+(x_i)$. Then each
16	$U_i$ is an open affine subset of $X$, and the $U_i$ cover $X$, so we can
17	compute the cohomology of $\mathcal{F}$ by using \v{C}ech cohomology for the
18	covering $\mathfrak{U} = (U_i)$, by (4.5). For any set of indices
19	$i_0, \ldots, i_p$, the open set $U_{i_0, \ldots, i_p}$ is just
20	$D_+(x_{i_0} \cdots x_{i_p})$, so by (II, 5.11) we have
21	\[
22	  \mathcal{F}(U_{i_0, \ldots, i_p}) \cong S_{x_{i_0} \cdots x_{i_p}},
23	\]
24	the localization of $S$ with respect to the element $x_{i_0} \cdots x_{i_p}$.
25	Furthermore, the grading on $\mathcal{F}$ corresponds to the natural grading
26	of $S_{x_{i_0} \cdots x_{i_p}}$ under this isomorphism. Thus the \v{C}ech
27	complex of $\mathcal{F}$ is given by
28	\[
29	  C^{\boldsymbol{\cdot}}(\mathfrak{U}, \mathcal{F}) :
30	    \prod S_{x_{i_0}} \to \prod S_{x_{i_0} x_{i_1}} \to \cdots \to
31	    S_{x_0 \cdots x_r},
32	\]
33	and the modules all have a natural grading compatible with the grading on
34	$\mathcal{F}$.
35	
36	Now $H^0(X, \mathcal{F})$ is the kernel of the first map, which is just $S$,
37	as we have seen earlier (II, 5.13). This proves (a).
38	
39	Next we consider $H^r(X, \mathcal{F})$. It is the cokernel of the last map
40	in the \v{C}ech complex, which is
41	\[
42	  d^{r-1} : \prod_k S_{x_0 \cdots \hat{x}_k \cdots x_r} \to
43	    S_{x_0 \cdots x_r}.
44	\]
45	We think of $S_{x_0 \cdots x_r}$ as a free $A$-module with basis
46	$x_0^{l_0} \cdots x_r^{l_r}$, with $l_i \in \mathbf{Z}$. The image of
47	$d^{r-1}$ is the free submodule generated by those basis elements for which
48	at least one $l_i \ge 0$. Thus $H^r(X, \mathcal{F})$ is a free $A$-module
49	with basis consisting of the ``negative'' monomials
50	\[
51	  \{ x_0^{l_0} \cdots x_r^{l_r} \mid l_i < 0 \text{ for each } i \}.
52	\]
53	Furthermore the grading is given by $\sum l_i$. There is only one such
54	monomial of degree $-r-1$, namely $x_0^{-1} \cdots x_r^{-1}$, so we see that
55	$H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-r-1))$ is a free $A$-module of rank $1$. This proves
56	(c).
57	
58	To prove (d), first note that if $n < 0$, then $H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n)) = 0$
59	by (a), and $H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-n-r-1)) = 0$ by what we have just seen,
60	since in that case $-n-r-1 > -r-1$, and there are no negative monomials of
61	that degree. So the statement is trivial for $n < 0$. For $n \ge 0$,
62	$H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(n))$ has a basis consisting of the usual monomials of
63	degree $n$, i.e., $\{ x_0^{m_0} \cdots x_r^{m_r} \mid m_i \ge 0 \text{ and }
64	\sum m_i = n \}$. The natural pairing with $H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-n-r-1))$
65	into $H^r(X, \mathcal{O}_X(-r-1))$ is determined by
66	\[
67	  (x_0^{m_0} \cdots x_r^{m_r}) \cdot (x_0^{l_0} \cdots x_r^{l_r}) =
68	    x_0^{m_0+l_0} \cdots x_r^{m_r+l_r},
69	\]
70	where $\sum l_i = -n-r-1$, and the object on the right becomes $0$ if any
71	$m_i + l_i \ge 0$. So it is clear that we have a perfect pairing, under
72	which $x_0^{-m_0-1} \cdots x_r^{-m_r-1}$ is the dual basis element of
73	$x_0^{m_0} \cdots x_r^{m_r}$.
74	\end{proof}

1	# Route decision — the mathematical architecture of the rebuild
2	
3	*2026-07-11, Fable-5 design session. Inputs: a 5-agent survey (mathlib v4.31.0 capability
4	inventory; old-draft map; Kleiman/FGA route DAG; alternative-routes survey; operational
5	lessons). Survey reports are archived in the session scratchpad; their load-bearing
6	conclusions are restated here so this document is self-contained.*
7	
8	This document fixes the route for all 14 protected targets in
9	`AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` and the design rules every wave must follow.
10	It is the map; the blueprint is the mathematics; the Lean tree is the proof.
11	
12	## 1. The route in one paragraph
13	
14	**`Jacobian C := Pic⁰_{C/k}`**, the identity component of the scheme representing the
15	étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of `C/k` (Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, FGA
16	Explained ch. 5). Representability is the central mountain (Grothendieck's Thm 4.8,
17	specialized hard to a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field).
18	The Albanese universal property is proved Milne-style (*Abelian Varieties* III.6.1):
19	symmetric powers `C^(g) → J` birational, rational maps into abelian varieties extend
20	(Milne I.3.2 = I.3.1 + Lemma 3.3), rigidity makes the factorization a homomorphism,
21	uniqueness descends from `k̄` to `k`. The genus is `g(C) := dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` with
22	`H¹` the derived-functor cohomology of the Zariski site of `C` valued in `ModuleCat k`,
23	computed by a pinned 2-affine-cover Mayer–Vietoris cokernel and proved finite by the
24	two-lattice ladder over a finite map `C → ℙ¹`. Every functorial target (`functor`,
25	`baseChangeIso`, the coherences) is a uniqueness-of-representing-object corollary of a
26	single pinned `RepresentableBy` datum — never a `Classical.choice` extraction.
27	
28	Why not the alternatives (survey verdicts):
29	
30	- **Weil group-chunk construction (Sym^g + birational group law): rejected.** Its
31	  obligations (scheme quotients by finite groups, relative divisors,
32	  cohomology-and-base-change, Weil's globalization theorem, plus a descent problem for
33	  pointless curves — the challenge's `Jacobian` takes **no rational point**) meet or
34	  exceed the FGA debt, and the functorial targets would still have to be re-derived
35	  through the Pic functor afterwards (Milne III.7.6). FGA's Thm 4.8 needs no point;
36	  that is a structural advantage for this exact statement file.
37	- **Kleiman's own Albanese derivation (`rmk:Alb`): rejected** — it outsources dual
38	  abelian varieties, autoduality (`Ĵ ≅ J`, [EGK Thm 2.1], unproved in our references)
39	  and projectivity of abelian varieties. Milne III.6.1 is strictly lighter and its
40	  ingredients (Sym^g, Riemann–Roch) are shared with the `Div^d`-representability leg,
41	  so their cost is amortized.
42	
43	## 2. Ground truth about mathlib v4.31.0 (verified in the checkout, not from memory)
44	
45	**Gifts to design around** (all present):
46	
47	- Group objects: `GrpObj`, bundled `Grp C`, `Functor.mapGrp/mapGrpIdIso/mapGrpCompIso/
48	  mapGrpNatIso` — the challenge's vocabulary, complete. **`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`**:
49	  a representing object of a group-valued functor gets `GrpObj` for free.
50	- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`: `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`
51	  (proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative) — the
52	  rigidity *corollary* is already a theorem.
53	- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`: `smooth_of_grpObj` (geometrically reduced +
54	  locally finite type group scheme over a field ⇒ smooth) — kills the deformation-theory
55	  half of smoothness; what remains of `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` is
56	  `T₀J ≅ H¹(C,𝒪_C)` plus dimension bookkeeping.
57	- `Sites/Representability.lean` (Zariski sheaf glued from representable opens is
58	  representable, Stacks 01JJ), `subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, the étale/fppf/fpqc sites.
59	- `ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`: `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the
60	  finite-map-to-ℙ¹ leg shrinks.
61	- Sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H` via `Ext` + Grothendieck-abelian `HasExt`/`EnoughInjectives`
62	  + the Mayer–Vietoris LES (`Sites/SheafCohomology/`) — at `AddCommGrpCat`; the
63	  `ModuleCat k` twin is ours to build (de-risked: the old draft did it).
64	- `IsProper`/`SmoothOfRelativeDimension`/`Geometrically*` with exactly the stability
65	  instances the frozen file consumes; valuative criterion over arbitrary valuation rings;

67	  `RingTheory/Invariant` (`A^G`); rational maps (`Birational/RationalMap.lean` — no

69	
70	**Load-bearing absences** (each is ours to build; nothing above Layer A of the DAG exists):

77	DVR refinement of the valuative criterion; genus (zero hits in all of Mathlib).

79	## 3. Definitions of record (the semantic pins)
80	
81	- **genus**: `genus C := Module.finrank k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` where `Hⁿₖ(C, F)` is the
82	  Ext-based cohomology of the (essentially small) Zariski site of `C` with values in
83	  `ModuleCat k`, applied to the structure sheaf viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules.
84	  *Not* a Čech-carrier definition: the derived definition is canonical
85	  (cover-independent by construction), mathlib-idiomatic, and the MV (0,1)-slice
86	  gives the 2-cover cokernel computation as a theorem, gate-free (old draft proved
87	  this bridge end to end; we re-derive it).
88	- **Jacobian**: the representing object of the degree-0 part of the étale-sheafified
89	  relative Picard functor, carried as a **pinned `RepresentableBy` datum** (data, not
90	  `Nonempty`), from which `instGrpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, `functor.map` is
91	  precomposition of represented functors, and `baseChangeIso` + coherences are
92	  uniqueness-of-representing-object arguments.
93	- **ofCurve**: the Abel–Jacobi map `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` via graph divisors
94	  (`Div¹_{C/k} = C`), landing in `Pic⁰` because `C` is connected and `P ↦ 0`.
95	- **Albanese UP**: Milne III.6.1 over `k̄`, descended to `k` uniqueness-first
96	  (Milne 6.4-pattern). Note the challenge asks uniqueness among **plain** `Over`-morphisms;
97	  rigidity converts any competitor into a homomorphism (it is pointed:
98	  `η ≫ g = P ≫ ofCurve P ≫ g = P ≫ f = η`), and homomorphisms agreeing on the
99	  generating curve agree.

186	## 5. Design rules (binding for every wave; distilled from the campaign post-mortems)
187	
188	1. **Keystone funnel.** Every wave funnels to one keystone with a wide parallel base;

193	   statements; each cost runs). Counterexamples for rejected pins go in the blueprint.

195	   classes or explicit structure hypotheses; `sorry` never inhabits a def/instance.

197	   defined through the same `RepresentableBy` datum; coherences become uniqueness.

199	   no Quot schemes.** Each is a measured multi-week detour whose consumers have
200	   cheaper curve-specific substitutes.

202	   1-to-1 nodes, `\leanok` only after kernel check; `\source{}` only after reading.**

205	   is a false oracle (lakefile sets `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`).
206	8. **Uniform genus.** No genus-0 fork anywhere; `J = Pic⁰` uniformly (the old draft
207	   deleted a weeks-long genus-0 lane).

5	import Mathlib
6	
7	/-!
8	# `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology and the structure sheaf as a sheaf of modules
9	
10	This file provides the cohomology carrier for the genus lane of the Jacobian challenge:
11	
12	1. For a small site `(C, J)` and a commutative ring `R`, the degree-`n` cohomology
13	   `Sheaf.HModule F n` of a sheaf `F` of `R`-modules, defined as the `Ext`-group from the
14	   constant sheaf with value `R` to `F` (mirroring `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, which is
15	   `AddCommGrpCat`-valued; ours is `ModuleCat R`-valued so that `Module.finrank` applies).
16	   Each `Sheaf.HModule F n` is an `R`-module via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf
17	   category, and `Sheaf.HModule.map` gives `R`-linear functoriality in `F`.
18	2. The degree-zero identification `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ : HModule F 0 ≃ₗ[R] F(⊤)`
19	   via `Ext⁰ ≅ Hom` and the constant-sheaf adjunction, together with its naturality.
20	3. For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, the structure sheaf of `X` as a sheaf of `k`-modules
21	   `Scheme.moduleKSheaf` on the small Zariski site `Opens.grothendieckTopology X`, by
22	   restriction of scalars along the structure morphism, with definitional (`rfl`) access
23	   to its sections and restriction maps.
24	
25	## Universe discipline
26	
27	Everything is single-universe: `k : Type u`, `X : Scheme.{u}`, the site `Opens X : Type u`
28	with hom-types in `Type u`, and coefficients `ModuleCat.{u} k`. Then
29	`Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat.{u} k)` is Grothendieck abelian relative
30	to `u` (`ModuleCat.{u} k` is, and the site is small), hence `HasExt.{u}` holds and
31	`Sheaf.HModule F n : Type u` with a `Module k` structure — no universe bump anywhere, so
32	`Module.finrank k` applies directly downstream.
33	
34	## Design notes
35	
36	* `Sheaf.HModule` is an `abbrev` for `Abelian.Ext`, so the entire mathlib `Ext` API
37	  (long exact sequences `Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁/₂/₃`, `Ext.extClass`, the
38	  Mayer–Vietoris machinery of `CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology`) applies
39	  transparently; we do not rebuild any of it.
40	* No global `Algebra k Γ(X, U)` instance is introduced (it would overlap with mathlib's
41	  `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instance via the tautological `OverClass X X`); the module
42	  structure is carried by the explicit defs `Scheme.overAlgebraMap`/`Scheme.overModule`
43	  and, where needed, `attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule`.
44	-/
45	
46	set_option autoImplicit false
47	
48	universe u
49	
50	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
51	
52	namespace CategoryTheory
53	
54	namespace Sheaf
55	
56	variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
57	
58	section HModule
59	
60	variable (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
61	  [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
62	
63	/-- The constant sheaf of `R`-modules with value `R` on the site `(C, J)`; sheaf cohomology
64	of sheaves of `R`-modules is `Ext` out of this object. -/
65	noncomputable def constModuleSheaf : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R) :=
66	  (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)
67	
68	variable {J R}
69	
70	/-- The degree-`n` cohomology of a sheaf of `R`-modules on a small site, as an `Ext`-group
71	in the Grothendieck abelian category `Sheaf J (ModuleCat R)`. It is a `Type u` carrying a
72	`Module R` instance (via the `R`-linear structure of the sheaf category). -/
73	noncomputable abbrev HModule (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℕ) : Type u :=
74	  Abelian.Ext (constModuleSheaf J R) F n
75	
76	namespace HModule
77	
78	variable {F G G' : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
79	
80	/-- Functoriality of `Sheaf.HModule` in the sheaf, as an `R`-linear map. -/
81	noncomputable def map (f : F ⟶ G) (n : ℕ) : HModule F n →ₗ[R] HModule G n :=
82	  (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f).postcompOfLinear R (constModuleSheaf J R) (add_zero n)
83	
84	lemma map_apply (f : F ⟶ G) {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
85	    map f n x = x.comp (Abelian.Ext.mk₀ f) (add_zero n) := rfl
86	
87	@[simp]
88	lemma map_id_apply {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) : map (𝟙 F) n x = x := by
89	  simp [map_apply]
90	
91	lemma map_comp_apply (f : F ⟶ G) (g : G ⟶ G') {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
92	    map (f ≫ g) n x = map g n (map f n x) := by
93	  simp [map_apply]
94	
95	instance [Injective F] (n : ℕ) : Subsingleton (HModule F (n + 1)) :=
96	  subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x ↦ x.eq_zero_of_injective
97	
98	end HModule
99	
100	section LinearEquivZero
101	
102	variable {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T)
103	
104	/-- The hom-equivalence of the constant-sheaf ⊣ global-sections adjunction, upgraded to an
105	`R`-linear equivalence. -/
106	noncomputable def constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
107	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
108	    ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] (M ⟶ F.obj.obj (op T)) := by
109	  refine
110	    { toFun := (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F
111	      invFun := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).symm
112	      left_inv := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).left_inv
113	      right_inv := ((constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F).right_inv
114	      map_add' := fun f g ↦ ?_
115	      map_smul' := fun r f ↦ ?_ } <;>
116	  · simp only [Adjunction.homEquiv_apply]
117	    ext v
118	    rfl
119	
120	lemma constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_apply (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
121	    {F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) :
122	    constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M F φ =
123	      (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv M F φ := rfl
124	
125	lemma constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_naturality (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
126	    {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
127	    (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj M ⟶ F) (f : F ⟶ G) :
128	    constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M G (φ ≫ f) =
129	      constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT M F φ ≫ f.hom.app (op T) := by
130	  simp only [constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv_apply]
131	  exact (constantSheafAdj J (ModuleCat.{u} R) hT).homEquiv_naturality_right φ f
132	
133	variable (J) in
134	/-- Morphisms out of the constant sheaf `R` compute global sections, `R`-linearly:
135	`Hom(R_X, F) ≃ₗ[R] F(⊤)`. -/
136	noncomputable def constModuleSheafHomEquiv (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
137	    (constModuleSheaf J R ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] F.obj.obj (op T) :=
138	  (constantSheafAdjHomLinearEquiv hT (ModuleCat.of R R) F).trans
139	    (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv.trans (LinearMap.ringLmapEquivSelf R R _))
140

142	    (φ : constModuleSheaf J R ⟶ F) (f : F ⟶ G) :
143	    constModuleSheafHomEquiv J hT G (φ ≫ f) =
144	      f.hom.app (op T) (constModuleSheafHomEquiv J hT F φ) := by

1	\chapter{The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve}
2	\label{chap:Challenge}
3	
4	Throughout, \(k\) is a field and \(C\) a \emph{smooth curve} over \(k\): a geometrically
5	irreducible, smooth \(k\)-scheme of relative dimension one, proper over \(k\). We write
6	\(C \to \Spec k\) for its structure morphism. This chapter states the goal of the project — the
7	genus, the Jacobian, the Abel--Jacobi map, and the universal property that characterizes the
8	Jacobian as the Albanese variety of \(C\). It is the mathematical counterpart of the statement file
9	\texttt{AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean}.
10	
11	\emph{Provenance.} Each node below should carry a \verb!\source{...}! anchor to the reference it is
12	read from once that reference has been consulted; anchors are added during the rebuild, never
13	guessed.
14	
15	\section{Genus}
16	
17	\begin{definition}[Genus]
18	  \label{def:genus}
19	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.genus}
20	  \leanok
21	  \uses{def:moduleKSheaf, def:HModule}
22	  The \emph{genus} of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is
23	  \[
24	    g(C) \;=\; \dim_k H^1\!\bigl(C, \struct C\bigr),
25	  \]
26	  the \(k\)-dimension of the first cohomology group of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf
27	  of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski site of \(C\) (Definition~\ref{def:moduleKSheaf}),
28	  with cohomology the \(\Ext\)-groups from the constant sheaf
29	  (Definition~\ref{def:HModule}).
30	\end{definition}
31	
32	\section{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}
33	
34	\begin{definition}[Jacobian]
35	  \label{def:jacobian}
36	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian}
37	  The \emph{Jacobian} \(\Jac(C)\) of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is the identity
38	  component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the relative Picard scheme of \(C\) over \(k\): the \(k\)-scheme
39	  representing (the fppf-sheafification of) the functor of degree-zero line bundles on \(C\).
40	\end{definition}

# χ-ledger lane — pre-design ground truth (run 0025, session 0002)

*Scouting notes for Wave-2 item 7 (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`, interface (E-i)–(E-iv) pinned in
`wave3-picard-design.md` §6.1). Not yet a binding design; recorded so the eventual designer does
not re-derive the codebase facts below.*

## Ground truth (verified in the tree, 2026-07-11)

- `Sheaf.HModule' F U n` (`Cohomology/OverOpen.lean:268`) is `Abelian.Ext (freeModuleSheaf J R U) F n`
  — Ext **on the whole site** from the free sheaf on `U`. It is NOT slice cohomology of `U`
  by definition.
- The landed affine vanishing `IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`
  (`Cohomology/AffineVanishing.lean:309`) is proved **for the structure sheaf specifically**
  (Serre cobounding through `cokernel_app_surjective`, which manipulates `Γ`-sections of
  `moduleKSheaf` over basic opens). There is no general "vanishing for any sheaf iso to 𝒪 on
  the affine" statement in the tree.
- Consequence: §6.1's remark that for a 2-cover twisted sheaf `F_g` the instances
  `Subsingleton (HModule' F_g Vᵢ 1)` "transport along `F_g|Vᵢ ≅ 𝒪|Vᵢ`" is NOT a rewrite;
  a restricted iso does not act on whole-site Ext. Three honest options:
  1. **Slice comparison lemma** (mathlib-PR grade, reusable): `Ext^n_{Sh(X)}(j_! A, F) ≃
     Ext^n_{Sh(U)}(A, F|_U)` for the open embedding `j : U ↪ X` (exact `j_!`, restriction
     preserving injectives). Then restricted isos transport vanishing. Clean, one-time cost.
  2. **Re-run Serre cobounding for `F_g`**: generalize `cokernel_app_surjective` from
     `moduleKSheaf` to any `F` that is "invertible-glued" on the affine — inspect whether the
     proof only touches sections over opens `⊆ U` (if so, the restricted iso rewrites it).
  3. **Avoid sheaf-level twists in the χ-ledger entirely** (divisor-first, recommended below).
- `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (`TwoCover.lean:94`) is already general-coefficients: any
  `F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat k)` + the two Subsingleton instances.
- Mathlib's `Abelian.Ext` provides the covariant LES in the second argument (SES of sheaves ⇒
  LES of `HModule'`), so skyscraper dévissage is available without new machinery.

## Recommended shape (to be confirmed by the χ-design session)

Divisor-first, mirroring the classical curve theory and the (E-i) normalization:

- Realize `𝒪(D)` for an effective divisor `D` on the curve as the **subsheaf of the constant
  function-field sheaf** `K_C` cut by stalkwise order conditions (DVR stalks are landed:
  `Curve/StalksDVR.lean`), NOT as a cocycle twist. `𝒪 = 𝒪(0) ⊆ 𝒪(D)` with quotient a finite
  skyscraper of `k`-dimension `deg D` (local colengths; finite flat rank of `𝒪_D` gives (E-i)).
- `h⁰/h¹/χ` of these subsheaves via whole-site `HModule` + the Ext LES on
  `0 → 𝒪(D′) → 𝒪(D) → (skyscraper) → 0`; finiteness inherited from the landed
  `Module.Finite k H¹(C,𝒪)` by dévissage; `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪) + deg D` by additivity. `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`
  from `Γ(C,𝒪)=k` + the genus definition.
- (E-ii) hom property + well-definedness on classes: through L2's meromorphic bridge (every
  class is a divisor-class difference) + "principal divisors have degree 0" (order-sum of a
  rational function vanishes — the one genuinely new arithmetic input; Weil repartition /
  two-chart argument over `ℙ¹` via the landed finite `π : C → ℙ¹` is the candidate route).
- (E-iv) field-extension invariance: via `Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean` (lane L3, in
  flight this session) + flat `⊗[k] K` exactness on the two-term complexes.
- The cocycle ↔ divisor interface stays in L2 (`DivisorClass.lean`/`MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`);
  the χ-ledger never needs `Subsingleton (HModule' F_g Vᵢ 1)` on this route — option 3 above,
  and the §6.1 coordination note to Wave 2 becomes moot.

---
name: horizon-commit
description: Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
---

Commit your work yourself, semantically, as you finish coherent pieces — don't
leave one giant undifferentiated snapshot for the system to sweep up. Good
commits are how the dashboard's change view and a human reviewer understand what
each session actually did.

## How

Use the Horizon CLI (never raw `git` on the ledger — the workspace repo is
out-of-tree with excludes, a secret guard, and provenance trailers that a bare
`git` would bypass):

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<message>" <files…>` — commit the files you changed.
  Paths are relative to your current directory (your project dir) or absolute.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<message>" --changed` — commit everything you
  changed in the project (excludes the shared Horizon state, which the system
  commits separately).

Provenance (run / session / role / task / projects) is stamped automatically —
do **not** pass it. The commit is attributed to your role.

## Messages — math first

Write the message the way you'd tell a mathematician what you did: the result
and the idea, in human-readable prose with LaTeX where it helps; mention Lean
declaration names / files only as supporting detail. Mirror the house style,
e.g. `Prove H^i(X,F)=0 for i>dim X via the Čech-to-derived comparison`. One
coherent step per commit; split unrelated work into separate commits.

## Concurrency — you are not alone

Other runs may be committing to the **same** ledger at the same time. That's
fine and intended (it helps everyone converge faster):

- Commits are a single shared branch — they serialise and never conflict as a
  git *merge*; if `horizon commit` hits contention it already retried, so trust
  its result.
- Commit only the files **you** changed. On a shared worktree your commit can
  still capture another run's in-flight edit to the same file — that's expected
  and acceptable; the message + trailers still record your intent.
- Never `reset`, `rebase`, force-push, or otherwise rewrite the ledger. `horizon
  commit` only ever appends a commit.

## When

Commit at each coherent milestone (a lemma closed, a file completed), not only

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dual.Defs
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Finite.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.IsBaseChangeFree
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.IsBaseChangeHom
/-!
# Base change for the dual of a module

* `Module.Dual.congr` : equivalent modules have equivalent duals.

If `f : Module.Dual R V` and `Algebra R A`, then

* `Module.Dual.baseChange A f` is the element
  of `Module.Dual A (A ⊗[R] V)` deduced by base change.

* `Module.Dual.baseChangeHom` is the `R`-linear map
  given by `Module.Dual.baseChange`.

* `IsBaseChange.dual` : for finite free modules, taking dual commutes with base change.

-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Module.Dual

open TensorProduct LinearEquiv

variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
  {V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module R V]
  {W : Type*} [AddCommMonoid W] [Module R W]
  (A : Type*) [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]

/-- Equivalent modules have equivalent duals. -/
@[simps!] def congr (e : V ≃ₗ[R] W) :
    Dual R V ≃ₗ[R] Dual R W := congrLeft R R e

/-- `LinearMap.baseChange` for `Module.Dual`. -/
def baseChange : Dual R V →ₗ[R] Dual A (A ⊗[R] V) :=
  (AlgebraTensorModule.rid R A A).compRight R ∘ₗ LinearMap.baseChangeHom R A V R

@[simp]
theorem baseChange_apply_tmul (f : Dual R V) (a : A) (v : V) :

66	## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier
67	
68	**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
69	`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
70	coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
71	remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
72	`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).
73	
74	**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
75	mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
76	functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
77	"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
78	candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
79	relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
80	`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.
81	
82	### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens
83	
84	```lean
85	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
86	structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
87	  opens : X → X.Opens
88	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
89	```
90	
91	with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
92	
93	Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):
94	
95	- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
96	  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
97	  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
98	  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
99	  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
100	  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
101	  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
102	  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
103	  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
104	  (pullback collapses indices).
105	- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
106	  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
107	  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
108	  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.
109	
110	### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`
111	
112	**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:
113	
114	```lean
115	/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
116	def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
117	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
118	-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
119	-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)
120	
121	abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
122	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
123	```
124	
125	Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
126	mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
127	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
128	with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
129	classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
130	are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
131	`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
132	`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:
133	
134	```lean
135	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
136	def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
137	    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
138	    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
139	    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
140	lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
141	```
142	
143	Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
144	CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):
145	
146	- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
147	  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
148	  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
149	  uses commutativity).
150	- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`
151	  (on cocycles: restrict values along the inclusions; strictly functorial:
152	  `res_res : res h₂ ∘ res h₁ = res (h₁.trans h₂)` holds on the nose at cochain level).
153	
154	### 2.3 The refinement colimit
155	
156	```lean
157	/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
158	def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
159	  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
160	    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
161	```
162	
163	- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
164	  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
165	  choice-free.
166	- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
167	  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
168	- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
169	  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
170	- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
171	  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
172	  `CechPic (Spec (.of K)) ≃* PUnit`-style triviality for fields (one-point space, one cover,
173	  `ev_refl` kills every cocycle) — this is Lane 1's cheap end-to-end test.
174	
175	### 2.4 Group structure: multiplicative, `CommGrpCat`-valued
176	
177	**Decision: multiplicative.** Justification (each item load-bearing):
178	
179	1. The cocycle values are *units of rings*; their native structure is multiplicative, and
180	   `tensor product of line bundles = pointwise multiplication of transition units`,
181	   `dual = pointwise inverse` — recon lesson 1's entire point. An additive carrier would
182	   re-introduce a translation layer at exactly the spot the old draft burned.
183	2. `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` takes `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}` — multiplicative — and
184	   `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` is the canonical bridge. The old draft's
185	   `AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}` choice cost both a universe bump and an additive/multiplicative
186	   mismatch at the representability gate.
187	3. Mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1` layer (§2.2) is multiplicative.
188	
189	The `ℤ`-valued *degree* (§6) is additive; the interface between the multiplicative Pic and the
190	additive degree is a single `→ ℤ` map with `deg (a * b) = deg a + deg b` — pinned as such, no
191	`Multiplicative ℤ` gymnastics in consumer-facing statements.
192	
193	### 2.5 Functoriality: pullback of cocycles
194	
195	```lean
196	def Scheme.CechPic.map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic
197	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_id (X) : CechPic.map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id _
198	theorem Scheme.CechPic.map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
199	    CechPic.map (f ≫ g) = (CechPic.map f).comp (CechPic.map g)
200	```
201	
202	On representatives: pull the cover back pointwise through `f.base` (`x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`),
203	pull the units back through `f.app`, restrict. `map_comp` compares the covers
204	`(f ≫ g) ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x))` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ (g ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰 (g (f x)))` — equal opens
205	(`Scheme.preimage_comp`), with the value comparison through `Scheme.Hom.app_comp`; if defeq
206	friction appears, prove it through the refinement relation (both sides restrict to a common
207	refinement) rather than `eqToHom` surgery.
208	
209	### 2.6 Divisor classes as cocycles: the `𝒪(D)` constructor
210	
211	Three constructors, in dependency order. Sign convention (route §3, audited in §8):
212	a local-equation system `(fᵢ)` for an effective `D` produces the class of `𝒪(D)` with
213	transition units `g x y = f x / f y` on overlaps (trivialization of `𝒪(D)` on `𝒰x` by
214	multiplication by `f x`).
215	
216	**(a) Local-equation data → class** (`Picard/DivisorClass.lean`):
217	
218	```lean
219	/-- Local equations for an effective Cartier divisor, adapted to a pointed cover. -/
220	structure Scheme.LocalEquations (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
221	  cover : X.PointedCover
222	  eqn : ∀ x, Γ(X, cover.opens x)
223	  regular : ∀ x, /- eqn x is a nonzerodivisor in every stalk over cover.opens x -/
224	  ratio_isUnit : ∀ x y, IsUnit (/- (eqn x)/(eqn y) as a section on the overlap, i.e.
225	      ∃ u : unit on 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y, (eqn x)|∩ = u * (eqn y)|∩ -/)
226	
227	def Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass (d : X.LocalEquations) : X.CechPic
228	  -- the class of the cocycle (x,y) ↦ the unit u x y with (eqn x)|∩ = u x y • (eqn y)|∩
229	```
230	
231	with: uniqueness of `u x y` (regularity makes the ratio unit unique — this is why `regular` is
232	part of the data), the cocycle identity for `u` (from associativity of the ratios),
233	*independence*: two `LocalEquations` cutting out the same closed subscheme (or related by
234	unitwise rescaling) have equal `picClass`; *multiplicativity*: pointwise product of equations ↦
235	product of classes; *pullback compatibility*: for `f : X' ⟶ X` such that the pulled-back
236	equations are still regular (guaranteed in the relative situation below),
237	`(d.pullback f).picClass = CechPic.map f d.picClass`.
238	
239	**(b) The two geometric instances** (`Picard/GraphDivisor.lean`):
240	
241	- *Point divisor.* For a `k`-point `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C`, the image of `P` is an
242	  effective Cartier divisor on `C.left`: the local ring at the image point is a DVR
243	  (`Curve/StalksDVR.lean`, Wave 1), so a uniformizer spreads to a local equation, and away from
244	  the point the equation `1` works. Output: `pointDivisor P : C.left.LocalEquations` (cover:
245	  a distinguished pointed cover; the choice of uniformizer is data *inside* the construction,
246	  with `picClass`-level independence proven — see the choice-discipline note in §4.4).
247	- *Graph divisor.* The diagonal `Δ ⊂ (C ⊗ C).left` is a relative effective divisor over the
248	  **second** factor: `pr₂|Δ` is an isomorphism onto the base, in particular finite flat of rank
249	  1, and smoothness of `C/k` of relative dimension 1 makes the conormal module invertible, so
250	  the ideal of `Δ` is locally one regular equation. Deliverable:
251	
252	  ```lean
253	  def graphLocalEquations (t : T ⟶ C /- in Over (Spec k) -/) :
254	      ((C ⊗ T).left).LocalEquations   -- local equations for Γ_t := (C ◁ t)-pullback of Δ ⋯
255	  theorem graphLocalEquations_base_change ⋯  -- Γ_{t ∘ g} equations = pullback of Γ_t equations
256	  ```
257	
258	  The base-change stability is *by construction*: `Γ_t` is the pullback of the universal `Δ`
259	  along `C ◁ (t ≫ ⋯)`, and (a)'s pullback compatibility applies because `Δ` is a *relative*
260	  divisor over the test factor (fibers never contain a component of `C`), so regularity
261	  survives every base change. Rank certificate: `𝒪_{Γ_t} ≅ 𝒪_T` as `T`-algebras, so the
262	  finite-flat rank of `Γ_t → T` is 1 — the input for the degree of `abelElement` (§6).
263	  This mathematics is Kleiman `ex:DivC` (§3.8: `X₀ = Div¹_{X/S}` for the smooth locus) and
264	  `rmk:Jac` (§5.26: "Given `t : T → X`, its graph subscheme `Γ_t ⊂ X × T` is a relative
265	  effective divisor"); both read.
266	
267	**(c) The meromorphic bridge** (`Picard/MeromorphicTrivialization.lean`; needed by the degree,
268	see §6.1): for `X` *integral*, every `CechPic` class is a divisor class. Cocycle proof shape:
269	every nonempty open contains the generic point; fix a base index `x₀` and localize the cocycle
270	values `g x x₀` into the function field; these are meromorphic local equations for a Cartier
271	divisor whose class is the given one. (Classical statement: Kleiman quotes it in the proof of
272	`th:qpp&p` (§5.4): "Since `X × T` is integral, there is a divisor `D` such that `𝒪(D) = 𝓛`
273	by [Hartshorne, Ex. II 6.15]".) This file also pins `divisorClass` for *differences*
274	`D₁ − D₂` of effective data as `picClass D₁ * (picClass D₂)⁻¹`.

278	## 3. (B) The relative functor
