355	### 4.2 The three options, weighed
356	
357	**(i) Hand-rolled plus-construction.** Define
358	`PicEt(T) := colim_{étale covers T'→T} ker(relPic T' ⇉ relPic (T' ×_T T'))` (equalizer form —
359	the plus needs no triple-overlap condition). One plus yields a sheaf iff the input presheaf is
360	separated; `relPic` **is** étale- (even fppf-) separated by Kleiman 2.5(1), whose hypothesis
361	holds by `ex:gc&r`. Cost: the separatedness proof (a genuine descent argument, §4.4), cover
362	smallness/indexing, colimit plumbing. Benefit: construction-canonical, evaluates concretely,
363	`relPic → PicEt` is a unit map usable everywhere, and over test schemes where a section exists
364	the unit is bijective *as a theorem* (2.5(2) recast) — exactly what Wave 4 needs over `k'`.
365	
366	**(ii) Define `PicEt` only via 2.5-comparison where sections exist + descent data elsewhere.**
367	Rejected. A piecewise definition is either non-canonical (it depends on which case a test
368	scheme falls into, and for `baseChangeIso` the case-split differs between `C/k` and `C_L/L`)
369	or secretly equal to (i) with the plus spelled out by hand. Every interface (group law, degree,
370	functoriality in `C`, base-field shuffle) would need case-coherence lemmas. The *content* of
371	(ii) — the comparison bijections — survives as the pair of theorems (C1), (C2) in §4.4.
372	
373	**(iii) Representability over `k'` + Galois descent, with `PicEt := the functor J represents`.**
374	Rejected **as a definition**, retained **as the Wave-4 proof strategy**. The blocker is
375	exactly the one the route anticipates: `baseChangeIso` must compare `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}`,
376	and both must be recognized as representing *the same construction-canonical functor* over `L`.
377	If `PicEt_k` is defined as `Hom(−, J)`, the `RepresentableBy` datum is a tautology carrying no
378	information, and the comparison of `(J_C)_L` with `J_{C_L}` has no common third functor to
379	factor through — one would have to smuggle the construction back in, per-instance, at every
380	coherence. **Resolution (binding):** the functor is defined by construction (option (i)); the
381	`k'`-plus-descent argument is how Wave 4 *produces* the `RepresentableBy` datum; after Wave 4,
382	nothing downstream ever unfolds `J`, only the datum.

384	### 4.3 The decision, in two layers
385	
386	**Layer 1 — affine tests, presented covers** (`Picard/EtaleCovers.lean`, `Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).
387	
388	For `T` with `T.left` affine (`A := Γ(T.left, ⊤)`), an étale cover index is a *presentation*:
389	
390	```lean
391	/-- A presented affine étale cover of `Spec A`: a chosen finite presentation of an étale,
392	faithfully flat `A`-algebra. -/
393	structure EtCover (A : CommRingCat.{u}) : Type u where
394	  n m : ℕ
395	  relations : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A
396	  -- carrier B := (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) ⧸ (span of relations)
397	  etale : Algebra.Etale A B
398	  surjective : /- Spec B → Spec A surjective (with étale + fp this gives faithful flatness) -/
399	```
400	
401	- `Type u`-small by construction, choice-free, and closed under the operations the plus needs:
402	  a *refinement* of covers is a `T`-morphism `Spec B' → Spec B`; *directedness* via
403	  `B ⊗[A] B'` (which has an explicit presentation); *base change* along `A → A'` re-presents
404	  with the same polynomials.
405	- Descent classes and the one-step plus, equalizer form:
406	
407	```lean
408	def descentClasses (E : EtCover A) : Subgroup (relPic C (T' E)) :=
409	  -- ker of (pullback along pr₁) / (pullback along pr₂) into relPic C (T' E ⊗_T T' E)
410	def PicEtAff (T /- affine -/) : Type u :=
411	  -- Σ (E : EtCover A), descentClasses E, quotiented by refinement, CommGroup
412	def picEtAffUnit : relPic C T →* PicEtAff C T   -- classes with the tautological descent datum
413	```
414	
415	- *Refinement-map independence* (the lemma that makes the colimit canonical): two `T`-morphisms
416	  `h₁ h₂ : Spec B'' → Spec B'` induce the same map on `descentClasses`, because
417	  `(h₁, h₂) : Spec B'' → Spec B' ×_T Spec B'` pulls the descent-datum equation
418	  `p₁^*λ = p₂^*λ` back to `h₁^*λ = h₂^*λ`. One line, but it is the keystone of
419	  well-definedness; pin it as a named lemma.
420	- Zariski refinements are included automatically: a standard affine cover
421	  `Spec (∏ᵢ A_{fᵢ}) → Spec A` is a presented étale cover, so the plus also performs the
422	  Zariski sheafification on affines — needed for `relPic`-vs-`PicEt` comparisons to be honest.
423	- Over a *field* base `Spec K`, single-factor refinement works (any factor field of an étale
424	  `K`-algebra already covers the point), so **field-extension covers are cofinal** — pin this
425	  lemma; it makes `PicEtAff C (Spec K) = colim_{K'/K fin. sep.} (Galois-stable part of
426	  relPic over K')`, the form the degree (§6) and Wave 4 consume.
427	
428	**Layer 2 — all test objects** (`Picard/PicEt.lean`).
429	
430	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` forces the functor to be defined on **all** of `Over (Spec (.of k))`
431	(the frozen `instGrpObj` leaves no choice), while the plus is only well-behaved on affines. The
432	extension is the canonical right-Kan-style limit over affine opens:
433	
434	```lean
435	def picEt (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
436	  -- lim over the poset of affine opens U ≤ T.left of PicEtAff C (T restricted to U),
437	  -- i.e. compatible families (λ_U)_U; CommGroup pointwise
438	def picEtFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}
439	def picEtUnit : relPicFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C
440	theorem picEt_affine_iso (hT : IsAffine T.left) : picEt C T ≃* PicEtAff C T ⋯
441	```
442	
443	For affine `T`, `T.left` is the top of its own affine-opens poset, so the limit collapses to
444	`PicEtAff C T` (canonical iso, not defeq — one lemma). Functoriality in `T` maps a family
445	`(λ_V)_V` over `T` to the family `(res λ_V)` indexed by pairs `U ⊆ f⁻¹V` — the comma-limit
446	construction. `picEt` is a Zariski sheaf by construction; the étale sheaf sequence is claimed
447	(and needed) **only for affine `T` with presented covers** — this is recorded as the honest
448	semantic pin in the blueprint: "`picEtFunctor` restricted to affine tests *is* the étale
449	sheafification of `relPicFunctor` there (one plus of a separated presheaf), and is its canonical
450	Zariski-continuous extension elsewhere." **OPEN-1**: whether Layer 2 is implemented as this
451	bespoke limit or through mathlib's dense-subsite machinery
452	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Affine.lean`: `isCoverDense_toOver_Spec` + `IsCoverDense` sheaf
453	extension); closing criterion in §9.

455	Also in `Picard/PicEt.lean`, stated at this level because Wave 7 consumes them:
456	
457	- `picEtMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) : picEtFunctor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C'` with `mapCurve_id/comp`
458	  (descend `relPicMapCurve` through the plus and the limit; pullback preserves descent data).

467	
468	**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
469	cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
470	restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
471	are shared bricks):
472	
473	1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
474	   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
475	   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
476	   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
477	2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
478	   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
479	   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
480	   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
481	3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
482	   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because
483	   `𝒪ˣ((C ⊗ V).left) = Γ(V)ˣ` by 2 (applied on an affine pointed cover of `T`). Hence the
484	   H_T-quotient loses nothing it shouldn't, and "which `N`" in a `pr^*N`-equation is unique.
485	4. `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean` (pure algebra, PR-candidate): along a faithfully flat ring
486	   map `A → B`, an invertible `B`-module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
487	   `A`-module, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism. (Survey: this exists **nowhere** in
488	   mathlib — "no effective descent of modules"; it is the honest algebraic core of both (C1)
489	   and (C2).)
490	5. Assembly (Kleiman's 2.5(1) argument recast): a class `λ ∈ relPic C T` dying on the cover
491	   gives, via 3 applied over `T'` and `T' ×_T T'`, a line-bundle class `n'` on `T'` with a
492	   descent datum along `Spec B → Spec A`; by 4 it descends to `n` on `T`, and `λ = pr^* n`
493	   follows from 3 again. Hence `λ = 0` in the quotient.

universe u₁ u₂ u v

open TensorProduct

/-- A ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S` is flat if `S` is flat as an `R` module. -/
@[algebraize Module.Flat]
def RingHom.Flat {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) : Prop :=
  letI : Algebra R S := f.toAlgebra
  Module.Flat R S

lemma RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] :
    (algebraMap R S).Flat ↔ Module.Flat R S := by
  rw [RingHom.Flat, toAlgebra_algebraMap]

namespace RingHom.Flat

variable {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]

variable (R) in
/-- The identity of a ring is flat. -/
lemma id : RingHom.Flat (RingHom.id R) :=
  Module.Flat.self

/-- Composition of flat ring homomorphisms is flat. -/
lemma comp {f : R →+* S} {g : S →+* T} (hf : f.Flat) (hg : g.Flat) : Flat (g.comp f) := by
  algebraize [f, g, (g.comp f)]
  exact Module.Flat.trans R S T

/-- Bijective ring maps are flat. -/
lemma of_bijective {f : R →+* S} (hf : Function.Bijective f) : Flat f := by
  algebraize [f]
  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (LinearEquiv.ofBijective (Algebra.linearMap R S) hf).symm

lemma containsIdentities : ContainsIdentities Flat := id

lemma stableUnderComposition : StableUnderComposition Flat := by
  introv R hf hg
  exact hf.comp hg

lemma respectsIso : RespectsIso Flat := by

# Stalks and specializations on a scheme with Dedekind section rings

A scheme covered by affine opens whose section rings are Dedekind domains behaves like a
smooth curve: its stalks are valuation rings (fields at generic points, DVRs at closed
points), and its specialization order has height one.  This file proves the pointwise
statements from the single hypothesis "`x` lies in an affine open with Dedekind section
ring", and derives the two consumers needed for the finite-fibers argument of the map to
`ℙ¹`:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.valuationRing_stalk`: the stalk at a point of an affine
  open with Dedekind section ring is a valuation ring.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq`: on an irreducible
  scheme, a generalization of such a point is the generic point or the point itself.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint`: on an irreducible,
  Noetherian scheme all of whose points have only trivial generalizations, a closed subset
  avoiding the generic point is finite.

Finally the hypotheses are discharged for a scheme smooth of relative dimension one over a
field, using the standard smooth charts and
`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain`:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section`,
* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.valuationRing_stalk`,
* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_section`.
-/

15	/-! # Base change properties for modules of linear maps
16	
17	* `IsBaseChange.linearMapRight`:
18	  If `M` is finite free and `P` is a base change of `N` to `S`,
19	  then `M →ₗ[R] P` is a base change of `M →ₗ[R] N` to `S`.
20	
21	* `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`:
22	  If `M` is finite free and `P` is a base change of `M` to `S`,
23	  if `Q` is a base change of `N` to `S`,
24	  then `P →ₗ[S] Q` is a base change of `M →ₗ[R] N` to `S`.
25	
26	* `IsBaseChange.end`:
27	  If `M` is finite free and `P` is a base change of `M` to `S`,
28	  then `P →ₗ[S] P` is a base change of `M →ₗ[R] M` to `S`.
29	
30	-/
31	
32	@[expose] public section
33	
34	namespace IsBaseChange
35	
36	open LinearMap TensorProduct Module
37	
38	variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
39	    (S : Type*) [CommSemiring S] [Algebra R S]
40	    (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
41	    {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
42	    {P : Type*} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module R P]
43	
44	section LinearMapRight
45	
46	variable [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
47	
48	/-- The base change homomorphism underlying `IsBaseChange.linearMapRight` -/
49	def linearMapRightBaseChangeHom (ε : N →ₗ[R] P) :
50	    (S ⊗[R] (M →ₗ[R] N)) →ₗ[S] (M →ₗ[R] P) where
51	  toAddHom := (TensorProduct.lift {
52	    toFun s := s • (LinearMap.compRight R ε (M := M))
53	    map_add' x y := by ext; simp [add_smul]
54	    map_smul' r s := by simp }).toAddHom
55	  map_smul' s x := by
56	    simp only [AddHom.toFun_eq_coe, coe_toAddHom, RingHom.id_apply]
57	    induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
58	    | zero => simp
59	    | add x y hx hy => simp [smul_add, hx, hy]
60	    | tmul t f => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', mul_smul]
61	
62	variable [Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
63	
64	variable {S}
65	
66	/-- The base change isomorphism underlying `IsBaseChange.linearMapRight` -/
67	noncomputable def linearMapRightBaseChangeEquiv
68	    {ε : N →ₗ[R] P} (ibc : IsBaseChange S ε) :
69	    S ⊗[R] (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] (M →ₗ[R] P) := by
70	  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective (linearMapRightBaseChangeHom S M ε)
71	  let b := Free.chooseBasis R M
72	  set ι := Free.ChooseBasisIndex R M
73	  have := Free.ChooseBasisIndex.fintype R M
74	  let e := (b.repr.congrLeft N R).trans (Finsupp.llift N R R ι).symm
75	  let f := (b.repr.congrLeft P S).trans (Finsupp.llift P R S ι).symm
76	  let h := linearMapRightBaseChangeHom S M ε
77	  let e' : S ⊗[R] (M →ₗ[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] (ι → N) :=
78	    LinearEquiv.baseChange R S (M →ₗ[R] N) (ι → N) e
79	  let h' := (f.toLinearMap.comp (linearMapRightBaseChangeHom S M ε)).comp e'.symm.toLinearMap
80	  suffices Function.Bijective h' by simpa [h'] using this
81	  suffices h' = (finitePow ι ibc).equiv by
82	    simp only [this]
83	    apply LinearEquiv.bijective
84	  suffices f.toLinearMap.comp (linearMapRightBaseChangeHom S M ε) =
85	      (finitePow ι ibc).equiv.toLinearMap.comp e'.toLinearMap by
86	    simp [h', this, ← LinearEquiv.trans_assoc e'.symm e']
87	  ext φ i
88	  simp
89	  simp [f, e', linearMapRightBaseChangeHom, LinearEquiv.baseChange, equiv_tmul,
90	    LinearEquiv.congrLeft, e]
91	
92	/-- If `M` has a finite basis and `P` is a base change of `N` to `S`,
93	then `M →ₗ[R] P` is a base change of `M →ₗ[R] N` to `S`. -/
94	theorem linearMapRight {ε : N →ₗ[R] P} (ibc : IsBaseChange S ε) :
95	    IsBaseChange S (LinearMap.compRight (M := M) R ε) := by
96	  apply of_equiv (linearMapRightBaseChangeEquiv M ibc)
97	  intro f
98	  simp [linearMapRightBaseChangeEquiv, linearMapRightBaseChangeHom]
99	
100	end LinearMapRight
101	
102	section LinearMapLeftRight
103	
104	variable {S M}
105	  {Q : Type*} [AddCommMonoid Q] [Module R Q]
106	  [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
107	  [Module S Q] [IsScalarTower R S Q]
108	
109	/-- The base change map for linear maps with source a free finite module. -/
110	noncomputable def linearMapLeftRightHom {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α)
111	    (β : N →ₗ[R] Q) :
112	    (M →ₗ[R] N) →ₗ[R] (P →ₗ[S] Q) :=
113	  ((LinearMap.llcomp (σ₂₃ := RingHom.id S) S P (S ⊗[R] M) Q).flip
114	    j.equiv.symm.toLinearMap) ∘ₗ
115	    (liftBaseChangeEquiv S).toLinearMap.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ
116	      (compRight R β (M := M))
117	
118	theorem linearMapLeftRightHom_apply
119	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (β : N →ₗ[R] Q) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (p : P) :
120	    linearMapLeftRightHom j β f p = ((liftBaseChangeEquiv S) (β ∘ₗ f)) (j.equiv.symm p) := by
121	  rfl
122	
123	@[simp] theorem linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply
124	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (β : N →ₗ[R] Q) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (m : M) :
125	    linearMapLeftRightHom j β f (α m) = β (f m) := by
126	  simp [linearMapLeftRightHom_apply, IsBaseChange.equiv_symm_apply]
127	
128	@[simp] theorem linearMapLeftRightHom_comp
129	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (β : N →ₗ[R] Q) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
130	    (linearMapLeftRightHom j β f).restrictScalars R ∘ₗ α = β ∘ₗ f := by
131	  ext; simp [linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply]
132	
133	variable [Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
134	
135	theorem linearMapLeftRight {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α)
136	    {β : N →ₗ[R] Q} (k : IsBaseChange S β) :
137	    IsBaseChange S (linearMapLeftRightHom j β) := by
138	  apply of_equiv <|
139	      (k.linearMapRight M).equiv ≪≫ₗ liftBaseChangeEquiv S ≪≫ₗ LinearEquiv.congrLeft Q S j.equiv
140	  intro f
141	  ext p
142	  simp [IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, LinearEquiv.congrLeft, linearMapLeftRightHom_apply]
143	
144	end LinearMapLeftRight
145	
146	section End
147	
148	variable {S M}
149	  [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
150	
151	/-- The base change map for endomorphisms of a free finite module. -/
152	noncomputable def endHom {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) :
153	    (M →ₗ[R] M) →ₗ[R] (P →ₗ[S] P) :=
154	  ((LinearMap.llcomp (σ₂₃ := RingHom.id S) S P (S ⊗[R] M) P).flip
155	    j.equiv.symm.toLinearMap) ∘ₗ
156	    (liftBaseChangeEquiv S).toLinearMap.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ
157	      (compRight R α (M := M))
158	
159	theorem endHom_apply
160	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (p : P) :
161	    endHom j f p = ((liftBaseChangeEquiv S) (α ∘ₗ f)) (j.equiv.symm p) := by
162	  rfl
163	
164	theorem endHom_comp_apply
165	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (m : M) :
166	    endHom j f (α m) = α (f m) := by
167	  simp [endHom_apply, IsBaseChange.equiv_symm_apply]
168	
169	theorem endHom_comp
170	    {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) :
171	    (endHom j f).restrictScalars R ∘ₗ α = α ∘ₗ f := by
172	  ext; simp [endHom_comp_apply]
173	
174	theorem endHom_one {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) :
175	    j.endHom 1 = 1 := by
176	  ext p
177	  induction p using j.inductionOn with
178	  | zero => simp
179	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
180	  | smul _ _ h => simp [h]
181	  | tmul m => simp [endHom_comp_apply]
182	
183	variable [Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
184	
185	theorem _root_.IsBaseChange.end {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) :
186	    IsBaseChange S (endHom j) := by
187	  apply of_equiv <|
188	      (j.linearMapRight M).equiv ≪≫ₗ liftBaseChangeEquiv S ≪≫ₗ LinearEquiv.congrLeft P S j.equiv
189	  intro f
190	  ext p
191	  simp [equiv_tmul, LinearEquiv.congrLeft, endHom_apply]
192	
193	end End
194	
195	section Matrix
196	
197	variable {Q : Type*} [AddCommMonoid Q] [Module R Q] [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
198	  [Module S Q] [IsScalarTower R S Q]
199	  {α : M →ₗ[R] P} {β : N →ₗ[R] Q}
200	  (ibcM : IsBaseChange S α) (ibcN : IsBaseChange S β)
201	  {ι θ : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] [Finite θ]
202	  (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (c : Module.Basis θ R N)
203	
204	theorem linearMapLeftRightHom_toMatrix (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
205	    (linearMapLeftRightHom ibcM β f).toMatrix (ibcM.basis b) (ibcN.basis c) =
206	      (f.toMatrix b c).map (algebraMap R S) := by
207	  ext i j
208	  simp only [toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply, basis_apply,
209	    linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply, basis_repr_comp_apply]
210	
211	theorem endHom_toMatrix (f : M →ₗ[R] M) :
212	    (endHom ibcM f).toMatrix (ibcM.basis b) (ibcM.basis b) =
213	      (f.toMatrix b b).map (algebraMap R S) := by
214	  ext i j
215	  simp only [toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply]
216	  simp only [basis_apply, endHom_comp_apply, basis_repr_comp_apply]
217	
218	
219	end Matrix
220	
221	section determinant
222	
223	variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
224	    (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
225	    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
226	    {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
227	
228	variable [Free R M] [Module.Finite R M]
229	
230	theorem det_endHom {α : M →ₗ[R] P} (j : IsBaseChange S α) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) :
231	    LinearMap.det (endHom j f) = algebraMap R S (LinearMap.det f) := by
232	  rcases subsingleton_or_nontrivial R with hR | hR
233	  · have : f = 1 := by
234	      have : Subsingleton M := Module.subsingleton R M
235	      exact Subsingleton.eq_one f
236	    simp [this, endHom_one]
237	  let b := Module.finBasis R M
238	  rw [← f.det_toMatrix b, ← (j.endHom f).det_toMatrix (j.basis b),
239	    endHom_toMatrix, ← RingHom.mapMatrix_apply, ← RingHom.map_det]
240	
241	end determinant

variable (X Y) in
theorem of_hasBinaryProduct' [HasBinaryProduct X Y] [HasTerminal C] :
    IsPullback Limits.prod.fst Limits.prod.snd (terminal.from X) (terminal.from Y) :=
  of_is_product (limit.isLimit _) terminalIsTerminal

theorem of_iso_pullback (h : CommSq fst snd f g) [HasPullback f g] (i : P ≅ pullback f g)
    (w₁ : i.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = fst) (w₂ : i.hom ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = snd) :
      IsPullback fst snd f g :=
  of_isLimit' h
    (Limits.IsLimit.ofIsoLimit (limit.isLimit _)
      (@PullbackCone.ext _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (PullbackCone.mk _ _ _) _ i w₁.symm w₂.symm).symm)

theorem of_horiz_isIso_mono [IsIso fst] [Mono g] (sq : CommSq fst snd f g) :
    IsPullback fst snd f g :=
  of_isLimit' sq
    (by
      refine
        PullbackCone.IsLimit.mk _ (fun s => s.fst ≫ inv fst) (by simp)
          (fun s => ?_) (by cat_disch)
      simp only [← cancel_mono g, Category.assoc, ← sq.w, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc, s.condition])

theorem of_horiz_isIso [IsIso fst] [IsIso g] (sq : CommSq fst snd f g) :
    IsPullback fst snd f g :=
  of_horiz_isIso_mono sq

lemma of_iso (h : IsPullback fst snd f g)
    {P' X' Y' Z' : C} {fst' : P' ⟶ X'} {snd' : P' ⟶ Y'} {f' : X' ⟶ Z'} {g' : Y' ⟶ Z'}
    (e₁ : P ≅ P') (e₂ : X ≅ X') (e₃ : Y ≅ Y') (e₄ : Z ≅ Z')
    (commfst : fst ≫ e₂.hom = e₁.hom ≫ fst')
    (commsnd : snd ≫ e₃.hom = e₁.hom ≫ snd')
    (commf : f ≫ e₄.hom = e₂.hom ≫ f')
    (commg : g ≫ e₄.hom = e₃.hom ≫ g') :
    IsPullback fst' snd' f' g' where
  w := by
    rw [← cancel_epi e₁.hom, ← reassoc_of% commfst, ← commf,
      ← reassoc_of% commsnd, ← commg, h.w_assoc]
  isLimit' :=
    ⟨(IsLimit.postcomposeInvEquiv
        (cospanExt e₂ e₃ e₄ commf.symm commg.symm) _).1
          (IsLimit.ofIsoLimit h.isLimit (by
            refine PullbackCone.ext e₁ ?_ ?_
            · change fst = e₁.hom ≫ fst' ≫ e₂.inv
              rw [← reassoc_of% commfst, e₂.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
            · change snd = e₁.hom ≫ snd' ≫ e₃.inv
              rw [← reassoc_of% commsnd, e₃.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]))⟩

/-- Same as `IsPullback.of_iso`, but using the data and compatibilities involving
the inverse isomorphisms instead. -/
lemma of_iso' (h : IsPullback fst snd f g)
    {P' X' Y' Z' : C} {fst' : P' ⟶ X'} {snd' : P' ⟶ Y'} {f' : X' ⟶ Z'} {g' : Y' ⟶ Z'}
    (e₁ : P' ≅ P) (e₂ : X' ≅ X) (e₃ : Y' ≅ Y) (e₄ : Z' ≅ Z)
    (commfst : e₁.hom ≫ fst = fst' ≫ e₂.hom)
    (commsnd : e₁.hom ≫ snd = snd' ≫ e₃.hom)
    (commf : e₂.hom ≫ f = f' ≫ e₄.hom)
    (commg : e₃.hom ≫ g = g' ≫ e₄.hom) :
    IsPullback fst' snd' f' g' := by
  apply h.of_iso e₁.symm e₂.symm e₃.symm e₄.symm
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commfst, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commsnd, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commf, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commg, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]

variable (X Y) in
theorem of_hasBinaryCoproduct' [HasBinaryCoproduct X Y] [HasInitial C] :
    IsPushout (initial.to _) (initial.to _) (coprod.inl : X ⟶ _) (coprod.inr : Y ⟶ _) :=
  of_is_coproduct (colimit.isColimit _) initialIsInitial

theorem of_iso_pushout (h : CommSq f g inl inr) [HasPushout f g] (i : P ≅ pushout f g)
    (w₁ : inl ≫ i.hom = pushout.inl _ _) (w₂ : inr ≫ i.hom = pushout.inr _ _) :
      IsPushout f g inl inr :=
  of_isColimit' h
    (Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoColimit (colimit.isColimit _)
      (PushoutCocone.ext (s := PushoutCocone.mk ..) i w₁ w₂).symm)

lemma of_iso (h : IsPushout f g inl inr)
    {Z' X' Y' P' : C} {f' : Z' ⟶ X'} {g' : Z' ⟶ Y'} {inl' : X' ⟶ P'} {inr' : Y' ⟶ P'}
    (e₁ : Z ≅ Z') (e₂ : X ≅ X') (e₃ : Y ≅ Y') (e₄ : P ≅ P')
    (commf : f ≫ e₂.hom = e₁.hom ≫ f')
    (commg : g ≫ e₃.hom = e₁.hom ≫ g')
    (comminl : inl ≫ e₄.hom = e₂.hom ≫ inl')
    (comminr : inr ≫ e₄.hom = e₃.hom ≫ inr') :
    IsPushout f' g' inl' inr' where
  w := by
    rw [← cancel_epi e₁.hom, ← reassoc_of% commf, ← comminl,
      ← reassoc_of% commg, ← comminr, h.w_assoc]
  isColimit' :=
    ⟨(IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv
        (spanExt e₁ e₂ e₃ commf.symm commg.symm) _).1
          (IsColimit.ofIsoColimit h.isColimit
            (PushoutCocone.ext e₄ comminl comminr))⟩

/-- Same as `IsPushout.of_iso`, but using the data and compatibilities involving
the inverse isomorphisms instead. -/
lemma of_iso' {Z X Y P : C} {f : Z ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {inl : X ⟶ P} {inr : Y ⟶ P}
    (h : IsPushout f g inl inr)
    {Z' X' Y' P' : C} {f' : Z' ⟶ X'} {g' : Z' ⟶ Y'} {inl' : X' ⟶ P'} {inr' : Y' ⟶ P'}
    (e₁ : Z' ≅ Z) (e₂ : X' ≅ X) (e₃ : Y' ≅ Y) (e₄ : P' ≅ P)
    (commf : e₁.hom ≫ f = f' ≫ e₂.hom)
    (commg : e₁.hom ≫ g = g' ≫ e₃.hom)
    (comminl : e₂.hom ≫ inl = inl' ≫ e₄.hom)
    (comminr : e₃.hom ≫ inr = inr' ≫ e₄.hom) :
    IsPushout f' g' inl' inr' := by
  apply h.of_iso e₁.symm e₂.symm e₃.symm e₄.symm
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commf, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← commg, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← comminl, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
  · simp only [Iso.symm_hom, Iso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, ← comminr, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]

18	  `Subsingleton (HModule' F_g Vᵢ 1)` "transport along `F_g|Vᵢ ≅ 𝒪|Vᵢ`" is NOT a rewrite;
19	  a restricted iso does not act on whole-site Ext. Three honest options:
20	  1. **Slice comparison lemma** (mathlib-PR grade, reusable): `Ext^n_{Sh(X)}(j_! A, F) ≃
21	     Ext^n_{Sh(U)}(A, F|_U)` for the open embedding `j : U ↪ X` (exact `j_!`, restriction

23	  2. **Re-run Serre cobounding for `F_g`**: generalize `cokernel_app_surjective` from

25	     proof only touches sections over opens `⊆ U` (if so, the restricted iso rewrites it).

27	- `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` (`TwoCover.lean:94`) is already general-coefficients: any
28	  `F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (ModuleCat k)` + the two Subsingleton instances.

5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf
6	
7	/-!
8	# Cohomology of an object of the site with `ModuleCat k` coefficients
9	
10	For a sheaf of `R`-modules `F` on a small site `(C, J)` and an object `U : C`, this file
11	defines the cohomology `Sheaf.HModule' F U n` of `U` with coefficients in `F`: the
12	`Ext`-group from the *free sheaf of `R`-modules on `U`* (the sheafification of the
13	composite `yoneda.obj U ⋙ ModuleCat.free R`) to `F`. This mirrors mathlib's
14	`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H'` (which is `AddCommGrpCat`-valued) at `ModuleCat R`, so that the
15	Mayer–Vietoris (0,1)-slice can be run `R`-linearly
16	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris`).
17	
18	## Main definitions
19	
20	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheaf J R U` — the free sheaf of `R`-modules on `U`.
21	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafMap J R i` — functoriality in `U`.
22	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafHomEquiv` — the `R`-linear "universal property of
23	  sections": `(freeModuleSheaf J R U ⟶ F) ≃ₗ[R] F(U)`, with naturality in `F`
24	  (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_comp`) and in `U` (`freeModuleSheafHomEquiv_map`).
25	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule' F U n` — `Ext^n(R[U], F)`, a `Type u` with a `Module R`
26	  structure.
27	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule'.linearEquiv₀` — `H'⁰(U, F) ≃ₗ[R] F(U)`.
28	* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.freeModuleSheafIsoConstModuleSheaf` — for a terminal object `T`,
29	  the canonical isomorphism `R[T] ≅ R_X` with the constant sheaf, whence
30	  `Sheaf.HModule.linearEquivHModule' : HModule F n ≃ₗ[R] HModule' F T n`: cohomology of
31	  the site (`Sheaf.HModule`) is cohomology of a terminal object.
32	
33	## Implementation notes
34	
35	Morphisms out of `freeModuleSheaf J R U` are computed from the sheafification universal
36	property (`sheafifyLift`) against the explicit presheaf morphism `freeModuleSheafDesc`
37	determined by a section `s ∈ F(U)`; no adjunction unfolding is needed. All elementwise
38	computations are routed through `ModuleCat.free_hom_ext` after a `change` to the
39	`ModuleCat.Hom.hom` spelling (the concrete-category coercion produced by `free_hom_ext`
40	is only defeq to it, and `rw` chokes on the mismatch otherwise). The whole file is
41	single-universe (`Type u` site, `ModuleCat.{u} R` coefficients), matching
42	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
43	-/

54	types is injective on finitely supported functions). Mirrors the mathlib instance for

9	/-!
10	# Degree-one cohomology vanishing on affine opens
11	
12	The keystone of the genus lane: for a scheme `X` over `Spec k` and an affine open
13	`U ≤ X`, the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski site,
14	has vanishing degree-one cohomology of `U`:
15	`Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule' (X.moduleKSheaf k) U 1)`
16	(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`), and for `X`
17	itself affine, vanishing degree-one cohomology of the site:
18	`Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1)`
19	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule_one`).
20	
21	## Proof architecture
22	
23	`H¹'(U) = Ext¹(k[U], 𝒪ₖ)` and `H¹ = Ext¹(k_X, 𝒪ₖ)` in the Grothendieck abelian category
24	of sheaves of `k`-modules, so it suffices to have
25	(`Abelian.Ext.subsingleton_one_of_injective_of_surjective`, proved here for any abelian
26	category with `HasExt`):
27	
28	* a monomorphism `ι : 𝒪ₖ ⟶ G` with `G` injective — supplied by `Injective.under`
29	  (the category is Grothendieck abelian, hence has enough injectives); and
30	* surjectivity of `Hom(L, G) ⟶ Hom(L, cokernel ι)` for `L = k[U]` resp. `L = k_X` —
31	  since morphisms out of `k[U]` (resp. `k_X`) compute sections over `U` (resp. `⊤`),
32	  this is surjectivity of `G(U) ⟶ (cokernel ι)(U)` on sections over the affine open
33	  (`IsAffineOpen.cokernel_app_surjective`), which is the geometric content:
34	
35	a section `q` of `cokernel ι` over `U` lifts locally to `G` (epimorphisms of sheaves are
36	locally surjective), on a finite cover of `U` by basic opens (affine opens are
37	quasi-compact); the differences of the local lifts are a Čech 1-cocycle with values
38	in `𝒪ₖ` (kernel-exactness of sections), which on an affine open is a coboundary
39	(`IsAffineOpen.exists_cech_cobounding`, Serre's argument); correcting the local lifts by
40	the coboundary makes them glue to a lift of `q` over `U`.
41	
42	No flasque/Godement machinery and no derived-functor comparison is needed: injectivity
43	enters only through `Ext¹(L, G) = 0` for `G` injective.
44	-/

57	
58	/-- Vanishing criterion for `Ext¹`: if `A` admits a monomorphism `ι` into an injective
59	object such that every morphism `L ⟶ cokernel ι` lifts along `cokernel.π ι`, then
60	`Ext¹(L, A) = 0`. -/
61	theorem subsingleton_one_of_injective_of_surjective {A I : C} (ι : A ⟶ I) [Mono ι]
62	    [Injective I] (L : C)
63	    (hsurj : ∀ φ : L ⟶ cokernel ι, ∃ ψ : L ⟶ I, ψ ≫ cokernel.π ι = φ) :
64	    Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext L A 1) := by
65	  suffices h : ∀ z : Abelian.Ext L A 1, z = 0 from ⟨fun x y ↦ (h x).trans (h y).symm⟩
66	  intro z
67	  have hS : (ShortComplex.mk ι (cokernel.π ι) (cokernel.condition ι)).ShortExact :=
68	    { exact := ShortComplex.exact_of_g_is_cokernel _ (cokernelIsCokernel ι) }
69	  have h1 : z.comp (mk₀ ι) (add_zero 1) = 0 := eq_zero_of_injective _
70	  obtain ⟨x₃, hx₃⟩ := covariant_sequence_exact₁ L hS z h1 (zero_add 1)
71	  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := hsurj (homEquiv₀ x₃)
72	  have hx₃' : mk₀ (ψ ≫ cokernel.π ι) = x₃ := by
73	    rw [hψ, mk₀_homEquiv₀_apply]
74	  calc z = x₃.comp hS.extClass (zero_add 1) := hx₃.symm
75	    _ = ((mk₀ ψ).comp (mk₀ (cokernel.π ι)) (zero_add 0)).comp hS.extClass (zero_add 1) := by
76	          rw [mk₀_comp_mk₀, hx₃']
77	    _ = (mk₀ ψ).comp ((mk₀ (cokernel.π ι)).comp hS.extClass (zero_add 1)) (zero_add 1) :=
78	          comp_assoc _ _ _ rfl rfl rfl
79	    _ = 0 := by rw [hS.comp_extClass]; simp

8	/-!
9	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
10	
11	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
12	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
13	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
14	modules:
15	
16	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
19	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
20	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
21	function spaces.
22	
23	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
24	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
25	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
26	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
28	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
33	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
34	* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
35	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
36	  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
37	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
38	* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
39	* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
40	  ("class of a section on the overlap").
41	* `TwoCover.h1CokEquiv : HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok k X U₀ U₁`.
42	* Compatibility: `h1CokEquiv_delta` (`h1CokEquiv ∘ delta = Quotient.mk`),
43	  `delta_surjective`, `delta_diff`, `delta_resHom_left/right` and
44	  `h1Cok_mk_resHom_left/right` (classes of sections extending to `U₀` or `U₁` vanish).
45	
46	The `k`-module structure on `Γ(X, U)` is `Scheme.overModule` (restriction of scalars
47	along the structure morphism), activated as a local instance as in
48	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf`.
49	-/

13	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` equipped with a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, this

16	the instance for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of the challenge, so that
17	`genus` is the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional vector space.

20	Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover`:
21	
22	* `V i := π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` is an affine open cover of `X`
23	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), so

25	* `N := Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` is a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]` through

---
name: horizon-waiting
description: How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
---

Your session is **one-shot and headless**. When you write your final report the
session ENDS and nothing calls you back. There is no notification when a
background job finishes, and any process you backgrounded is killed the moment
the session exits. So a plan like "kick off the build and wait to be notified"
silently fails: the notification never comes and the build dies with you.

Therefore, whenever a result you depend on is produced by a build, subagent,
monitor, or shell command:

- **Run it in the FOREGROUND and block on it.** Wait for it to finish and read
  its exit code / output within this session. A heavy `lake build` can take many
  minutes (sometimes 20+) — budget for that and wait it out; do not cut it short.
- If you must poll, **poll in a loop inside this session** until the work has
  definitively finished. Never end the session expecting to resume.

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	-/
5	import Mathlib
6	
7	/-!
8	# Curve substrate: basic consequences of the standing hypotheses
9	
10	The Jacobian challenge (`AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`) works with a bundle
11	`C : Over (Spec (.of k))` together with the instances `[IsProper C.hom]`,
12	`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]` and `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.
13	This file records the *topological and scheme-theoretic substrate* every later wave consumes,
14	as instances keyed on the `Over`-bundle:
15	
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_left_of_geometricallyIrreducible`:
17	  a scheme geometrically irreducible over a field is irreducible (in particular nonempty).
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_left_of_quasiCompact` and
19	  `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparatedSpace_left_of_quasiSeparated`:
20	  a scheme quasi-compact (resp. quasi-separated) over `Spec k` is a quasi-compact
21	  (resp. quasi-separated) topological space; both hypotheses hold for proper morphisms.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced`:
23	  a scheme geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over a field is integral.
24	  In particular Mathlib's function-field API (`Scheme.functionField`) applies to `C.left`.
25	
26	Geometric reducedness is taken as a *hypothesis* here: the implication
27	"smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced" is proved elsewhere in this project
28	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.GeometricallyReduced`), never in this file.
29	
30	Statements are given for an arbitrary `X : Over (Spec (.of k))` with the minimal hypotheses,
31	so that they also apply to the Jacobian bundle itself in later waves.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory Limits
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
43	
44	section OverField
45	
46	variable (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
47	
48	/-- A scheme geometrically irreducible over a field is irreducible.
49	In particular it is nonempty (`IrreducibleSpace.toNonempty`). -/
50	instance irreducibleSpace_left_of_geometricallyIrreducible
51	    [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] : IrreducibleSpace X.left :=
52	  GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton X.hom
53	
54	/-- A scheme quasi-compact over `Spec k` (e.g. proper) is a quasi-compact topological space. -/
55	instance compactSpace_left_of_quasiCompact [QuasiCompact X.hom] : CompactSpace X.left :=
56	  QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace X.hom
57	
58	/-- A scheme quasi-separated over `Spec k` (e.g. proper) is a quasi-separated topological
59	space. -/
60	instance quasiSeparatedSpace_left_of_quasiSeparated [QuasiSeparated X.hom] :
61	    QuasiSeparatedSpace X.left :=
62	  quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated X.hom
63	
64	/-- A scheme geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over a field is integral.
65	
66	Geometric reducedness is a hypothesis here; for the curve bundle of the challenge it is
67	supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project. -/
68	instance isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced
69	    [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom] [GeometricallyReduced X.hom] : IsIntegral X.left :=
70	  have : GeometricallyIntegral X.hom :=
71	    GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible X.hom
72	  GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton X.hom
73	
74	end OverField
75	
76	/-!
77	## Regression checks
78	
79	The remaining standing consequences of the hypothesis bundle are already provided by Mathlib
80	instances; the `example`s below pin them down so a Mathlib bump cannot silently lose them.
81	They are stated for the exact curve bundle of `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.
82	-/
83	
84	section RegressionChecks
85	
86	variable {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
87	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
88	
89	-- `IsProper` unfolds into separatedness, universal closedness and finite type,
90	-- and quasi-compactness/quasi-separatedness follow.
91	example : IsSeparated C.hom := inferInstance
92	example : UniversallyClosed C.hom := inferInstance
93	example : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
94	example : QuasiCompact C.hom := inferInstance
95	example : QuasiSeparated C.hom := inferInstance
96	
97	-- Geometric irreducibility makes the structure morphism surjective and the total space
98	-- an irreducible, nonempty, quasi-compact, quasi-separated topological space.
99	example : Surjective C.hom := inferInstance
100	example : IrreducibleSpace C.left := inferInstance
101	example : Nonempty C.left := inferInstance
102	example : CompactSpace C.left := inferInstance
103	example : QuasiSeparatedSpace C.left := inferInstance
104	
105	-- With geometric reducedness (supplied by smoothness elsewhere in this project), the curve is
106	-- integral and Mathlib's function field 𝒪_{C,η} carries its field structure and algebra maps.
107	example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] : IsIntegral C.left := inferInstance
108	noncomputable example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] : Field C.left.functionField := inferInstance
109	noncomputable example [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] (x : C.left) :
110	    Algebra (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField := inferInstance
111	
112	end RegressionChecks
113	
114	end AlgebraicGeometry
115

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	-/
5	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.DedekindSections
6	
7	/-!
8	# Stalks and specializations on a scheme with Dedekind section rings
9	
10	A scheme covered by affine opens whose section rings are Dedekind domains behaves like a
11	smooth curve: its stalks are valuation rings (fields at generic points, DVRs at closed
12	points), and its specialization order has height one.  This file proves the pointwise
13	statements from the single hypothesis "`x` lies in an affine open with Dedekind section
14	ring", and derives the two consumers needed for the finite-fibers argument of the map to
15	`ℙ¹`:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.valuationRing_stalk`: the stalk at a point of an affine
18	  open with Dedekind section ring is a valuation ring.
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq`: on an irreducible
20	  scheme, a generalization of such a point is the generic point or the point itself.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint`: on an irreducible,
22	  Noetherian scheme all of whose points have only trivial generalizations, a closed subset
23	  avoiding the generic point is finite.
24	
25	Finally the hypotheses are discharged for a scheme smooth of relative dimension one over a
26	field, using the standard smooth charts and
27	`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain`:
28	
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section`,
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.valuationRing_stalk`,
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_section`.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
43	
44	section Pointwise
45	
46	/-- The stalk of an integral scheme at a point of an affine open whose section ring is a
47	Dedekind domain is a valuation ring: the localization of a Dedekind domain at a prime is a
48	field (at `⊥`) or a discrete valuation ring (at a maximal ideal), and both are valuation
49	rings. -/
50	theorem IsAffineOpen.valuationRing_stalk [IsIntegral X] {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
51	    (hD : IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V)) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ V) :
52	    ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
53	  letI : Algebra Γ(X, V) (X.presheaf.stalk x) := X.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk ⟨x, hx⟩
54	  have hloc : IsLocalization.AtPrime (X.presheaf.stalk x) (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩).asIdeal :=
55	    hV.isLocalization_stalk ⟨x, hx⟩
56	  set q := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ with hq
57	  by_cases hbot : q.asIdeal = ⊥
58	  · -- At the generic point of `V` the stalk is the fraction field.
59	    have hsub : q.asIdeal.primeCompl = nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, V) := by
60	      ext z
61	      simp [Ideal.primeCompl, hbot, mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero]
62	    have hfrac : IsLocalization (nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, V)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
63	      rw [← hsub]
64	      exact hloc
65	    letI : Field (X.presheaf.stalk x) := IsFractionRing.toField Γ(X, V)
66	    infer_instance
67	  · -- At other points the stalk is a DVR.
68	    have : IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) :=
69	      IsLocalization.AtPrime.isDiscreteValuationRing_of_dedekind_domain Γ(X, V) hbot _
70	    infer_instance
71	
72	/-- On an irreducible scheme, a generalization of a point of an affine open with Dedekind
73	section ring is the generic point or the point itself: primes of a Dedekind domain below a
74	given prime are `⊥` or the prime itself. -/
75	theorem IsAffineOpen.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq [IrreducibleSpace X] {V : X.Opens}
76	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (hD : IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V)) {x y : X} (hx : x ∈ V)
77	    (h : y ⤳ x) : y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x := by
78	  have hy : y ∈ V := h.mem_open V.2 hx
79	  set py := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨y, hy⟩ with hpy
80	  set px := hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩ with hpx
81	  have hyx : hV.fromSpec.base py = y := hV.fromSpec_primeIdealOf ⟨y, hy⟩
82	  have hxx : hV.fromSpec.base px = x := hV.fromSpec_primeIdealOf ⟨x, hx⟩
83	  -- Transfer the specialization along the open immersion `Spec Γ(X, V) ⟶ X`.
84	  have hspec : py ⤳ px := by
85	    refine hV.fromSpec.isOpenEmbedding.isInducing.specializes_iff.mp ?_
86	    rw [hyx, hxx]
87	    exact h
88	  have hle : py.asIdeal ≤ px.asIdeal := (PrimeSpectrum.le_iff_specializes py px).mpr hspec
89	  by_cases hbot : py.asIdeal = ⊥
90	  · -- `y` is the image of the generic point of `Spec Γ(X, V)`.
91	    left
92	    have hgen : (genericPoint (Spec Γ(X, V)) : Spec Γ(X, V)) = py := by
93	      rw [genericPoint_eq_bot_of_affine]
94	      exact (PrimeSpectrum.ext hbot).symm
95	    rw [← hyx, ← hgen, genericPoint_eq_of_isOpenImmersion hV.fromSpec]
96	  · -- A nonzero prime of a Dedekind domain is maximal, so `py = px`.
97	    right
98	    have hmax : py.asIdeal.IsMaximal := py.isPrime.isMaximal hbot
99	    have : py.asIdeal = px.asIdeal := hmax.eq_of_le px.isPrime.ne_top hle
100	    rw [← hyx, ← hxx, PrimeSpectrum.ext this]
101	
102	end Pointwise
103	
104	section Finiteness
105	
106	/-- On an irreducible scheme whose specialization order has height one (every strict
107	generalization is the generic point), every non-generic point is closed. -/
108	theorem Scheme.isClosed_singleton_of_forall_specializes [IrreducibleSpace X]
109	    (hgen : ∀ x y : X, y ⤳ x → y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x) {x : X}
110	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) : IsClosed ({x} : Set X) := by
111	  have : closure ({x} : Set X) ⊆ {x} := by
112	    intro y hy
113	    have hxy : x ⤳ y := specializes_iff_mem_closure.mpr hy
114	    rcases hgen y x hxy with h | h
115	    · exact absurd h hx
116	    · exact h ▸ rfl
117	  exact closure_subset_iff_isClosed.mp this
118	
119	/-- **Finiteness of proper closed subsets of a curve-like scheme.**  On an irreducible,
120	Noetherian (as a topological space), sober scheme whose specialization order has height one,
121	a closed subset avoiding the generic point is finite: it is a finite union of irreducible
122	closed subsets, and each of these is the closure of a non-generic point, hence a singleton. -/
123	theorem Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint [IrreducibleSpace X]
124	    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
125	    (hgen : ∀ x y : X, y ⤳ x → y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x) {Z : Set X} (hZ : IsClosed Z)
126	    (hξ : genericPoint X ∉ Z) : Z.Finite := by
127	  obtain ⟨S, hSfin, hScl, hSirr, hSsup⟩ :=
128	    TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_finite_set_isClosed_irreducible hZ
129	  rw [hSsup]
130	  refine Set.Finite.sUnion hSfin fun t ht => ?_
131	  -- Each irreducible component of `Z` is the closure of a non-generic point, hence a
132	  -- singleton.
133	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := QuasiSober.sober (hSirr t ht) (hScl t ht)
134	  have hzZ : z ∈ Z := hSsup ▸ Set.mem_sUnion.mpr ⟨t, ht, hz.mem⟩
135	  have hzξ : z ≠ genericPoint X := fun h => hξ (h ▸ hzZ)
136	  have hcl : IsClosed ({z} : Set X) :=
137	    Scheme.isClosed_singleton_of_forall_specializes hgen hzξ
138	  have : t = {z} := by
139	    rw [← hz.def, hcl.closure_eq]
140	  rw [this]
141	  exact Set.finite_singleton z
142	
143	end Finiteness
144	
145	section SmoothCurve
146	
147	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
148	
149	/-- Every point of an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field lies in
150	an affine open whose section ring is a Dedekind domain: a standard smooth chart of relative
151	dimension `1`. -/
152	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section
153	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] (x : X) :
154	    ∃ V : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ x ∈ V ∧ IsDedekindDomain Γ(X, V) := by
155	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hsm⟩ :=
156	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := 1) (f := f) x
157	  -- The base affine open is nonempty, hence is all of the one-point space `Spec K`.
158	  have hUtop : U = ⊤ := by
159	    have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
160	      inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
161	    refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y => ?_)
162	    exact Subsingleton.elim (f.base x) y ▸ e hxV
163	  subst hUtop
164	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
165	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
166	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
167	  haveI : Nonempty V := ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩⟩
168	  algebraize [(f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom]
169	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain
170	    Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) Γ(X, V)⟩
171	
172	/-- The stalks of an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field are
173	valuation rings. -/
174	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.valuationRing_stalk
175	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] (x : X) :
176	    ValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
177	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hD⟩ :=
178	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section f x
179	  exact hV.valuationRing_stalk hD hxV
180	
181	/-- On an integral scheme smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field, the only
182	generalizations of a point are the generic point and the point itself. -/
183	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq
184	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] {x y : X} (h : y ⤳ x) :
185	    y = genericPoint X ∨ y = x := by
186	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, hD⟩ :=
187	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isDedekindDomain_section f x
188	  exact hV.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq hD hxV h
189	
190	/-- **Existence of a transcendental rational function.**  On an integral scheme smooth of
191	relative dimension `1` over a field `K`, the function field contains an element `f₀`
192	transcendental over `K`, where `K` acts on the function field through the structure morphism
193	(global sections followed by the germ at the generic point).
194	
195	The element is the étale coordinate of a standard smooth chart
196	(`Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental`). -/
197	theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental_functionField
198	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsIntegral X] :
199	    ∃ f₀ : X.functionField, ∀ P : Polynomial K, P ≠ 0 →
200	      Polynomial.eval₂ ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
201	        X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial).hom f₀ P ≠ 0 := by
202	  classical
203	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hxV, e, hsm⟩ :=
204	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := 1) (f := f)
205	      (genericPoint X)
206	  have hUtop : U = ⊤ := by
207	    have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
208	      inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
209	    refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y => ?_)
210	    exact Subsingleton.elim (f.base (genericPoint X)) y ▸ e hxV
211	  subst hUtop
212	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
213	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
214	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
215	  haveI : Nonempty V := ⟨⟨genericPoint X, hxV⟩⟩
216	  algebraize [(f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom]
217	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental
218	    Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) Γ(X, V)
219	  refine ⟨(X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom t, fun P hP => ?_⟩
220	  -- Rewrite the structure composite through the chart.
221	  have hcomp : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫
222	      X.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint X) trivial =
223	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ V e ≫
224	        X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV := by
225	    simp only [Scheme.Hom.appLE, Category.assoc]
226	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res (homOfLE e) _ hxV]
227	    rfl
228	  rw [hcomp]
229	  -- Unfold the composite evaluation into a germ of an `aeval` in the chart.
230	  have heval : Polynomial.eval₂ ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appLE ⊤ V e ≫
231	      X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom
232	        ((X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom t) P =
233	      (X.presheaf.germ V (genericPoint X) hxV).hom
234	        (Polynomial.aeval t (P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom)) := by
235	    rw [Polynomial.aeval_def, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, Polynomial.hom_eval₂,
236	      Polynomial.eval₂_map]
237	    rfl
238	  rw [heval]
239	  -- The germ map is injective on the integral scheme `X`, and `t` is transcendental.
240	  intro hzero
241	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom : K →+* _) :=
242	    ((ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
243	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv).mp inferInstance).injective
244	  have hmap : P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom ≠ 0 :=
245	    fun h0 => hP ((Polynomial.map_eq_zero_iff hinj).mp h0)
246	  refine ht ⟨P.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv.hom, hmap, ?_⟩
247	  refine germ_injective_of_isIntegral X (genericPoint X) hxV ?_
248	  rw [map_zero]
249	  exact hzero
250	
251	end SmoothCurve
252	
253	end AlgebraicGeometry

7	/-!
8	# Standard smooth algebras of relative dimension one over a field are Dedekind domains
9	
10	The commutative-algebra bricks for "the local rings of a smooth curve are discrete valuation
11	rings":
12	
13	* `IsDedekindDomainDvr.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType` /
14	  `IsDedekindDomain.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType`: a domain which is unramified and of
15	  finite type over a Dedekind domain is a Dedekind domain.  This generalizes Mathlib's
16	  `isDedekindDomain.of_formallyUnramified` from module-finite to finite-type algebras: the
17	  incomparability of primes, which for finite algebras comes from integrality, here comes from
18	  quasi-finiteness (`Algebra.QuasiFinite`, satisfied by any unramified algebra essentially of
19	  finite type).
20	* `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain`: a domain which is standard
21	  smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field is a Dedekind domain.  By the structure theorem
22	  for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7,
23	  `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_etale_mvPolynomial`), such an algebra is
24	  étale over the polynomial ring `k[t]`, which is a principal ideal domain; étale maps are
25	  unramified and of finite type, so the previous brick applies.
26	* `Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental`: a nontrivial standard
27	  smooth algebra of relative dimension `1` over a field contains an element transcendental over
28	  the field, namely the étale coordinate: étale algebras are flat, hence torsion-free over
29	  `k[t]`, so the coordinate satisfies no nonzero polynomial.
30	
31	Everything in this file is stated in Mathlib generality and is a candidate for upstreaming.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false

36	section Unramified
37	
38	/-- A domain which is unramified and of finite type over a Dedekind domain is a Dedekind
39	domain in the DVR sense: it is Noetherian, and its localization at every nonzero prime is a
40	discrete valuation ring.
41	
42	This generalizes `isDedekindDomainDvr.of_formallyUnramified` (which assumes the algebra to be
43	module-finite) to finite-type algebras: the incomparability of primes over a common prime of
44	the base, which for finite algebras follows from integrality, here follows from
45	quasi-finiteness of unramified algebras (`Algebra.QuasiFinite.eq_of_le_of_under_eq`). -/
46	theorem IsDedekindDomainDvr.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType
47	    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
48	    [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDomain B] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B] :
49	    IsDedekindDomainDvr B where
50	  __ := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing A B
51	  is_dvr_at_nonzero_prime := by
52	    intro q hq hqp
53	    let q' := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)
54	    suffices q'.IsPrincipal from ((IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE (Localization.AtPrime q)
55	      (IsLocalization.AtPrime.not_isField B hq (Localization.AtPrime q))).out 4 0).mp this
56	    let p := q.under A
57	    let _ := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p q
58	    -- Incomparability from quasi-finiteness: a nonzero prime of `B` contracts to a nonzero
59	    -- prime of `A`.
60	    have hp : p ≠ ⊥ := by
61	      intro hp0
62	      refine hq (Algebra.QuasiFinite.eq_of_le_of_under_eq (R := A) ⊥ q bot_le ?_).symm
63	      exact (le_bot_iff.mp (hp0 ▸ Ideal.comap_mono bot_le)).trans hp0.symm
64	    have : p.IsMaximal := (hqp.under A).isMaximal hp
65	    let _ : Field (A ⧸ p) := Ideal.Quotient.field p
66	    -- The fiber ring over `p` is finite over the residue field `A ⧸ p` by unramifiedness.
67	    have : Module.Finite (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ p.map (algebraMap A B)) :=
68	      Algebra.FormallyUnramified.finite_of_free _ _
69	    have := IsArtinianRing.of_finite (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ p.map (algebraMap A B))
70	    suffices q' = (p.map (algebraMap A B)).map (algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q)) by
71	      rw [this, Ideal.map_map, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq,
72	        IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq A (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q),
73	        ← Ideal.map_map]
74	      infer_instance
75	    rw [← (Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isRadical_map_isMaximal A B p).radical,
76	      IsLocalization.map_radical q.primeCompl,
77	      IsLocalization.AtPrime.radical_map_of_mem_minimalPrimes (Localization.AtPrime q) q,
78	      Localization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal]
79	    rw [Ideal.minimalPrimes_eq_comap]
80	    exact ⟨q.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (p.map (algebraMap A B))),
81	      IsArtinianRing.mem_minimalPrimes bot_le, Ideal.comap_map_mk Ideal.map_comap_le⟩
82	
83	/-- A domain which is unramified and of finite type over a Dedekind domain is a Dedekind
84	domain. -/
85	theorem IsDedekindDomain.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType
86	    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
87	    [IsDedekindDomain A] [IsDomain B] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B] :
88	    IsDedekindDomain B :=
89	  have := IsDedekindDomainDvr.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType A B
90	  inferInstance
91	
92	end Unramified

101	    IsPrincipalIdealRing (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) := by
102	  have e : Polynomial k ≃+* MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k :=
103	    (MvPolynomial.uniqueAlgEquiv k (Fin 1)).symm.toRingEquiv
104	  exact IsPrincipalIdealRing.of_surjective e.toRingHom e.surjective

113	/-- A domain which is standard smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field is a Dedekind
114	domain: by the structure theorem for standard smooth algebras (Stacks 00T7) it is étale over
115	the principal ideal domain `k[t]`, and unramified finite-type algebras over Dedekind domains
116	are Dedekind. -/
117	theorem Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isDedekindDomain [IsDomain B]
118	    [Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 k B] : IsDedekindDomain B := by
119	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_etale_mvPolynomial 1 k B
120	  algebraize [g.toRingHom]
121	  have : Algebra.Etale (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) B := hg.toAlgebra
122	  have := MvPolynomial.isDedekindDomain_fin_one k
123	  exact IsDedekindDomain.of_formallyUnramified_of_finiteType (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) B

125	/-- A nontrivial standard smooth algebra of relative dimension `1` over a field contains an
126	element transcendental over the field: the étale coordinate given by the structure theorem for
127	standard smooth algebras.  Its transcendence comes from flatness of étale maps: `B` is a
128	torsion-free `k[t]`-module, so no nonzero polynomial annihilates `1`. -/
129	theorem Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_transcendental [Nontrivial B]
130	    [Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 k B] :
131	    ∃ t : B, Transcendental k t := by
132	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_etale_mvPolynomial 1 k B
133	  algebraize [g.toRingHom]
134	  have : Algebra.Etale (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) B := hg.toAlgebra
135	  -- `B` is flat over `k[t]`, hence torsion-free, hence the algebra map is injective.
136	  have hinj : Function.Injective g := by
137	    intro a b hab
138	    by_contra hne
139	    have hmem : a - b ∈ nonZeroDivisors (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) :=
140	      mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero (sub_ne_zero_of_ne hne)
141	    have hreg := Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_of_nonZeroDivisors (M := B) hmem
142	    have : (a - b) • (1 : B) = (a - b) • (0 : B) := by
143	      rw [smul_zero, Algebra.smul_def, mul_one, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, map_sub,
144	        sub_eq_zero]
145	      exact hab
146	    exact one_ne_zero (hreg this)
147	  refine ⟨g (MvPolynomial.X 0), fun hX => ?_⟩
148	  -- If the coordinate were algebraic, `X 0` would be algebraic in `k[t]` itself.
149	  have : IsAlgebraic k (MvPolynomial.X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 1) k) := by
150	    obtain ⟨P, hP, hPeval⟩ := hX
151	    refine ⟨P, hP, hinj ?_⟩
152	    rw [map_zero, ← hPeval]
153	    exact (Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply g (MvPolynomial.X 0) P).symm
154	  exact MvPolynomial.transcendental_X k (0 : Fin 1) this
155	
156	end StandardSmooth

7	/-!
8	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
9	
10	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
11	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
12	
13	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
14	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
16	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
17	
18	## Proof sketch
19	
20	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
21	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
22	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
23	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
24	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
25	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
26	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
27	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
28	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
29	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
30	field is injective.
31	
32	Geometric reducedness enters only through `GeometricallyIntegral`; for the curve bundle of the
33	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Limits
41	
42	namespace CommRingCat
43	
44	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
45	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
46	
47	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
48	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
49	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
50	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
51	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
52	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
53	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
54	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
55	  -- the codiagonal
56	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
57	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
58	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
59	  have : IsIso μ := by
60	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
61	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
62	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
63	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
64	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
65	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
66	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
67	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
68	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
69	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
71	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
72	
73	end CommRingCat

77	/-- Bundled variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.isField_of_universallyClosed`: if `X` is an integral
78	scheme, universally closed over the spectrum of a (bundled) commutative ring `R` that is a
79	field, then `Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field. -/
80	theorem isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (hR : IsField R)
81	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec R) [IsIntegral X] [UniversallyClosed f] :
82	    IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := by
83	  let F := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ f.appTop
84	  have : F.hom.IsIntegral := by
85	    apply RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso.2 (e := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv)
86	    exact isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed f
87	  algebraize [F.hom]
88	  exact isField_of_isIntegral_of_isField' hR

90	/-- **Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field.**
91	If `X` is proper and geometrically integral over a field `K`, then the map on global sections
92	`Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` induced by the structure morphism is bijective; informally,
93	`Γ(X, 𝒪_X) = K`. -/
94	theorem bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
95	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
96	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
97	    Function.Bijective f.appTop := by
98	  have hX : IsIntegral X := GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton f
99	  -- `A := Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field, finite over `K`.
100	  have hA : IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := isField_of_universallyClosed K f
101	  letI : Field Γ(X, ⊤) := hA.toField
102	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
103	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
104	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
105	  refine ⟨f.appTop.hom.injective, ?_⟩
106	  -- Surjectivity: `f.appTop` is a finite epimorphism.
107	  suffices h : Epi f.appTop from
108	    RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite f.appTop (finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed K f)
109	  -- Base change to `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)`.
110	  set q : Spec Γ(X, ⊤) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K) :=
111	    Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop) with hq
112	  -- The total space of the base change is integral, so its global sections form a field.
113	  have hsub : Subsingleton ↥(Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) :=
114	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤)))
115	  have hYint : IsIntegral (pullback f q) :=
116	    GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton (pullback.snd f q)
117	  have hUC : UniversallyClosed (pullback.snd f q) :=
118	    MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance
119	  have hD : IsField Γ(pullback f q, ⊤) :=
120	    isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField hA (pullback.snd f q)
121	  -- Flat base change of global sections: the pushout square.
122	  have hUST : (⊤ : (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).Opens) ≤ q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top q).ge
123	  have hUSX : (⊤ : X.Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top f).ge
124	  have hUY : (⊤ : (pullback f q).Opens) =
125	      pullback.fst f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ ⊓ pullback.snd f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := by simp
126	  have hCS : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
127	  have hQS : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
128	  have hiso := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
129	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY
130	    (isAffineOpen_top _) (isAffineOpen_top _)
131	    (by simpa using CompactSpace.isCompact_univ)
132	    (by simpa using isQuasiSeparated_univ)
133	  have hpo := (isIso_pushoutSection_iff
134	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY).mp hiso
135	  -- The two legs of the pushout square agree up to `ΓSpecIso`.
136	  have hcompat : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)).hom = f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX := by
137	    have h₁ : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST = q.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app q
138	    have h₂ : f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f
139	    rw [h₁, h₂, hq, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
140	  have hepi : Epi (f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX) :=
141	    CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField hpo hD (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)) hcompat
142	  rwa [show f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop from Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f] at hepi
143	
144	/-- Instance-friendly form of
145	`AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`. -/
146	theorem isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
147	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
148	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
149	    IsIso f.appTop :=
150	  (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr
151	    (bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral f)

155	/-- `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ k` for the curve bundle: the structure morphism of a proper, geometrically
156	irreducible, geometrically reduced scheme over `k` induces an isomorphism on global sections.
157

this is the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U)`.

This is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/
abbrev app (U : Y.Opens) : Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :=
  f.c.app (op U)

this is the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)`.

This is treated as a suffix in lemma names. -/

open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

universe v u

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)

/-- A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ Y` is flat if for each affine `U ⊆ Y` and
`V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U`, the induced map `Γ(Y, U) ⟶ Γ(X, V)` is flat. This is equivalent to
asking that all stalk maps are flat (see `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`).
-/
@[mk_iff]
class Flat (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop where
  flat_appLE (f) :
    ∀ {U : Y.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen U) {V : X.Opens} (_ : IsAffineOpen V) (e : V ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U),
      (f.appLE U V e).hom.Flat

alias Scheme.Hom.flat_appLE := Flat.flat_appLE

@[deprecated (since := "2026-01-20")] alias Flat.flat_of_affine_subset := Scheme.Hom.flat_appLE

namespace Flat

instance : HasRingHomProperty @Flat RingHom.Flat where
  isLocal_ringHomProperty := RingHom.Flat.propertyIsLocal
  eq_affineLocally' := by
    ext X Y f
    rw [flat_iff, affineLocally_iff_forall_isAffineOpen]

instance (priority := 900) [IsOpenImmersion f] : Flat f :=
  HasRingHomProperty.of_isOpenImmersion
    RingHom.Flat.containsIdentities

instance : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition @Flat :=
  HasRingHomProperty.stableUnderComposition RingHom.Flat.stableUnderComposition

@[simp]
lemma SpecMap_iff {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} {f : R ⟶ S} : Flat (Spec.map f) ↔ f.hom.Flat :=
  HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff

instance comp {X Y Z : Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [hf : Flat f] [hg : Flat g] : Flat (f ≫ g) :=
  MorphismProperty.comp_mem _ f g hf hg

instance : MorphismProperty.Respects @Flat @IsOpenImmersion where
  postcomp _ _ _ _ := inferInstance

instance : MorphismProperty.IsMultiplicative @Flat where
  id_mem _ := inferInstance

instance isStableUnderBaseChange : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange @Flat :=
  HasRingHomProperty.isStableUnderBaseChange RingHom.Flat.isStableUnderBaseChange

instance (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Flat g] : Flat (pullback.fst f g) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _ inferInstance

instance (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Flat f] : Flat (pullback.snd f g) :=
  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance

instance (f : X ⟶ Y) (V : Y.Opens) [Flat f] : Flat (f ∣_ V) :=
  IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.restrict ‹_› V

instance (f : X ⟶ Y) (U : X.Opens) (V : Y.Opens) (e) [Flat f] : Flat (f.resLE V U e) := by
  delta Scheme.Hom.resLE; infer_instance

lemma of_stalkMap (H : ∀ x, (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat) : Flat f :=
  HasRingHomProperty.of_stalkMap RingHom.Flat.ofLocalizationPrime H

lemma stalkMap [Flat f] (x : X) : (f.stalkMap x).hom.Flat :=
  HasRingHomProperty.stalkMap (P := @Flat)
    (fun f hf J hJ ↦ hf.localRingHom J (J.comap f) rfl) ‹_› x

/-!
# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
modules:

`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`

(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
function spaces.

**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).

## Main declarations

* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.
* `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — the general-coefficients form: for any sheaf `F` of
  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,
  `HModule F 1 ≃ₗ[k] F(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range(moduleDiff)` (reusable for twisted sheaves).
* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.
* `TwoCover.H1Cok k X U₀ U₁` — the cokernel carrier `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range diff`.
* `TwoCover.delta` — the connecting map `Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁) →ₗ[k] HModule (X.moduleKSheaf k) 1`
  ("class of a section on the overlap").
====

/-!
# The two-lattice finiteness lemma over Laurent polynomials

Let `k` be a commutative ring and `N` a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]`.
Suppose `Q₀ Q₁ : Submodule k N` satisfy:

* `Q₀` is stable under multiplication by `T` and contains a finite set spanning `N`
  over `k[T;T⁻¹]`;
* `Q₁` is stable under multiplication by `T⁻¹`, and every element of `N` lands in `Q₁`
  after multiplication by a sufficiently negative power of `T`.

Then the quotient `N ⧸ (Q₀ ⊔ Q₁)` is a finite `k`-module
(`LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_span_eq_top`).

The proof is the classical monomial ladder: pick a uniform `M` with `T ^ (-M) • xᵢ ∈ Q₁` for
the finitely many generators `xᵢ`; then `T ^ j • xᵢ` lies in `Q₀` for `j ≥ 0`, in `Q₁` for
`j ≤ -M`, and only the finite window `-M < j < 0` survives modulo `Q₀ + Q₁`.

This is the pure-algebra engine behind the finiteness of the coherent cohomology
`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of a curve `C` equipped with a finite morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`: apply it to
`N = Γ(π⁻¹D₊(x₀) ⊓ π⁻¹D₊(x₁))` with `Q₀, Q₁` the images of the sections over the two chart
preimages, so that `N ⧸ (Q₀ ⊔ Q₁)` computes `H¹` by Mayer–Vietoris.

## Main results

* `LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_span_eq_top`: the keystone, with the
  first lattice hypothesis given by an explicit finite spanning set inside `Q₀`.
* `LaurentPolynomial.moduleFinite_quotient_sup_of_exists_smul_mem`: the symmetric
  localization form: both lattice hypotheses phrased as "surjectivity up to powers of `T`"

lemma lTensor_exact [Flat R M] ⦃N N' N'' : Type*⦄
    [AddCommGroup N] [AddCommGroup N'] [AddCommGroup N''] [Module R N] [Module R N'] [Module R N'']
    ⦃f : N →ₗ[R] N'⦄ ⦃g : N' →ₗ[R] N''⦄ (exact : Function.Exact f g) :
    Function.Exact (f.lTensor M) (g.lTensor M) := by
  let π : N' →ₗ[R] N' ⧸ LinearMap.range f := Submodule.mkQ _
  let ι : N' ⧸ LinearMap.range f →ₗ[R] N'' :=
    Submodule.subtype _ ∘ₗ (LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange g).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      Submodule.quotEquivOfEq (LinearMap.range f) (LinearMap.ker g)
        (LinearMap.exact_iff.mp exact).symm
  suffices exact1 : Function.Exact (f.lTensor M) (π.lTensor M) by
    rw [show g = ι.comp π from rfl, lTensor_comp]
    exact exact1.comp_injective _ (lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap ι <| by
      simpa [ι, -Subtype.val_injective] using Subtype.val_injective) (map_zero _)
  exact _root_.lTensor_exact _ (fun x ↦ by simp [π]) Quotient.mk''_surjective

    Function.Exact (f.rTensor M) (g.rTensor M) := by
  let π : N' →ₗ[R] N' ⧸ LinearMap.range f := Submodule.mkQ _
  let ι : N' ⧸ LinearMap.range f →ₗ[R] N'' :=
    Submodule.subtype _ ∘ₗ (LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange g).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      Submodule.quotEquivOfEq (LinearMap.range f) (LinearMap.ker g)
